description: Work instructions for processing all deduction types for ADUSA Distribution — The Giant Company, Giant Foods, and Stop & Shop. Covers customer general info, signon job aid, deduction types (Off Invoice, Billback, Scan, TPR, Post Audit, Advantage Billing, and more), contract/POP validation, and client-specific instructions for 30+ clients.

sections.title: CUSTOMER GENERAL INFORMATION
sections.content:
Customer Invoice Info:
Is line level detail indexed on the customer’s documentation (customer invoice, customer check request, unsaleable/spoils, post audit, EDI 812/820) or client deduction notice if one of these documents is included? YES
To determine the division refer to the Buyer Code identifier on the customer invoice:
NXXX = ADUSA Stop & Shop - SSAHNE
NSPI = ADUSA Stop & Shop post audit (internal)
NCNL = ADUSA Stop & Shop post audit (external)
GXXX = ASUSA The Giant Company - AHOLPH
GSPI = ASUSA The Giant Company post audit (internal)
GSPL = ASUSA The Giant Company post audit (external)
LXXX = ADUSA Giant Foods - GIANBW
LSPI – ADUSA Giant Foods post audit (internal)
LSPL = ADUSA Giant Foods post audit (external)
LCNL = ADUSA Giant Foods post audit (internal)
If the week being billed falls within dates shown on two events (the dates crossover), then the claim will need to be escalated so the Sales team can identify with how they want us to proceed.
GC/SSNE on an invoice means The Giant Company (Previously Giant Carlisle).
P-Vendor information can be found in the C&S SOP
FEES: Invoice #s ending in an F are C&S fees charged for deducting on behalf of Ahold. There is no contract for the C&S service fee. Ahold sends C&S invoices in batches of 10 which determines the fee that C&S will charge. Refer to the C&S SOP for how the fees are calculated. Client specifc information on fee processing can also be found in the C&S SOP. Refer to the Servce Fees section for additional information Service Fees.
If a fee has been deducted for any invalid invoice in the batch of 10, the following policy for repayment of these fees is below:
$150.00 – Ahold will not repay.
5% - Ahold will repay 5% of the total value of the invalid invoice only.
$1000 – Ahold will pro rate the amount of the repay based on the total of all invoices.
Private label, to identify a customer invoice as private label the REFERENCE field will begin with PRV or PV.
Freetown, Chester and Jessup:
When C&S deducts on half of Ahold and the above divisions are present they relate to the Ahold divisions listed below:
Freetown & Chester, Stop & Shop SSAHNE
Jessup, Giant Food Landover GIANBW
P-Deal or P-Vendor:
When C&S deducts on behalf of Ahold and P-Deal or P-Vendor is present on the C&S customer invoice, refer to the C&S SOP for instruction.
AHOLD BILL PAYER PROGRAM (pre-paid program):
The Ahold Bill Payer Agreement (BPA) program is similar to a checking account for clients’ trade spending. The client determines the types of billings they want to apply to the BPA and then deposits funds according to their forecasted spend for the quarter, period or year. Once the fund has been activated with the first deposit, invoices generated that have been selected on the Agreement are systematically applied to the client’s BPA.
Bill Payer prepaid claims claims create from the customer invoice.
For clients who agree to go on the Bill Payer program, an agreement is signed between the client representative and AHOLD. Below are copies of a blank agreement form and explanation of the various Billing Types seen on the form.
Advantage Billing:
No contract or POP is required.
No client event number will be available. Claims should be sent to the client for internal clearing.
Above instructions apply if no client-specific instruction is available.
PXX refers to the period, or timeframe, that Ahold is billing for.
Warehouses that are listed on Ahold invoices and which locations those warehouses support:
The below example may be found in AR as Customer Invoice doc type. However, it is not a deduction – it is a notification of a deduction being applied to the pre-paid account. Claims created from this document should be closed in AR and not processed.
Contract Info:
Acoustic DemandTec contracts for all Ahold Divisions will be found by searching under customer sign on: AHOLDMST.
Two contracts are created for Stop & Shop; one for NE and one for NY. If unsure which one to use, link the S&S NE contract to the claim.
When alerting for a missing Acoustic DemandTec/VPF Contract: Add the alpha code “AUSA” IN FRONT of the numeric portion of the Acoustic DemandTec# in the check # field. Example: “AUSA123456”.
Stock Protection on a contract usually means Floorstock Protection. However, if a contract has verbiage like “Cost Difference” it could mean many other things. With this verbiage, sales must be alerted to provide the exact type of offer made.
Comments at the bottom of the contract can be useful for claims validation and breakdown.
POP Info:
In order to determine all of the items to be included for POP review the contract. Ahold lists only one item per rate on their invoices for Scans and Lump Sums.The data on the contract will assist in locating POP; therefore, the contract should be located before the POP is pulled.
Ad
It is at the discretion of the Category Manager at AHOLD whether or not an ad will run, even if an ad is mentioned on the contract. If no ad is found, POP-IRI data will be acceptable proof of performance needed for that claim. This is for all promotion types except Ad Lump Sum.
Ad dates run Saturday thru Thursday.
Spin Reports
Spin reports are updated weekly and provide volume for one week based on a Saturday week ending date.
The Ahold spins are required when the client requires a customer spin run for POP
Use the following criteria to search the spin reports in ACOSTA Relay.
Client Sign-on: RPTCLIEN
Customer Sign-on: AHOLPH
Doc Type: POP Movement/TPR - 7
Client Ref #: Week End Date (Saturday) MM/DD/YYYY
Customer Ref#: RAW – Report Type (Example: RAW – PERISHABLE)
RAW – NON PERISHABLE: Contains frozen, grocery, and refrigerated items.
RAW – PERISHABLE: Contains meat, deli, and other perishable related items.
Both the Perishable and Non-Perishable reports should be checked for relevant data if any client data is missing. Ahold is moving from C&S to Direct Warehouses, and is now placing direct warehouse spins for all clients on the Perishable report.
How to Read RAW – NON PERISHABLE:
Units shipped during this periodUnits shipped during this periodCases shipped during this periodCases shipped during this periodClient nameClient namePack sizePack sizeAhold Item Number as appears on customer invoiceAhold Item Number as appears on customer invoiceWeek end dateWeek end dateDivisionDivisionProducts descriptionProducts descriptionUPC code of this productUPC code of this productItem sizeItem sizeClient name in C&S system. This can be used if unsure what the vendor name is from the Ahold Vendor NameClient name in C&S system. This can be used if unsure what the vendor name is from the Ahold Vendor Name
How to Read RAW – PERISHABLE Reports:
Cases shipped during this periodCases shipped during this periodWeek end dateWeek end dateItem sizeItem sizePack sizePack sizeProduct descriptionProduct descriptionUPC CodeUPC CodeAhold item number. Most of the time Ahold drops the ‘0’s when referencing this number on the customer invoice and contractAhold item number. Most of the time Ahold drops the ‘0’s when referencing this number on the customer invoice and contractDivisionDivisionClient nameClient name
GCC Spin Process: If an Ahold/all banners claim requires their spin report for validation please use the 5, 7 & 10 rule for searching for the spin. 5, 7 & 10 rule: If spins are not available, note the line ‘pending performance’. On day 5 and & if not available, note the line ‘pending performance’. If the spin is not available on day10 step to the CRA.
The 5, 7 & 10 rule applies to ATB claims only.
Any priority claims would take precedence over the 5, 7 & 10 day rule.
Fines:
Deal Accuracy Fines
For beverage brands at Stop and Shop:
There will be nuisance fees associated with inaccurate deal submission. This will be effective with deals starting 11/1/24
Fee schedule below:
First Offense - $500
Second Offense - $1,000
Third Offense - $1,500
Fourth and any subsequent - $5,000
Other General Info:
Price change lead time is 90 days from the day the price change is submitted via email.

sections.title: CLIENT SPECIFIC VALIDATION INFORMATION
sections.content:
BARILLA
Shopper Marketing contracts that state “Meat Rack Program” or “Marketing” on them are Shoppers Marketing, see example below and process per Client SOP.
When an invoice is for Plus, Gluten Free or Collezione and has no breakdown, use the following percentages to breakdown the claim. Barilla does not want all funds applied to just one. Use one UPC from each PPG to create the DBW.
Gluten Free57%
Plus28%
Collezione15%
Invoices with MDM are cleared to Shopper Marketing. Refer to Barilla SOP for clearing and validating instructions.
Peapod at home shoppers program lump sum: This may not always be listed on the contract. If it is listed the claim amount does not have to match the amount that is on the contract.
Peapod Shoppers Marketing Invoice will say either “1st/2nd half” have a high dollar lump sum amount, as well as “Peapod Preferred Partner Agreement". See example below:
Ahold scan invoices are no longer billed by division. The claim should be linked to one division's VPF and the remaining division contracts should be linked within this VPF.
Load to Card is Shopper Marketing and is cleared to YN04.
CSM Redemption Invoices are cleared to Shopper Marketing. Invoices should be sent to Barilla to clear internally.
2% Ecomm deductions and Advantage Billing deductions are cleared internally by client.
BEIERSDORF
Fairshare 2025 Billing: Program clear to Non-Promo 2025 for C&S – N25CSW004 – YS72 – Enabler (incl. Cust HQ Fee).
Fairshare 2026 Billing: Program clear to Non-Promo 2026 for C&S – N26CSW001 – YS72 – Enabler (incl. Cust HQ Fee).
BUSH
Bush is on the Bill Payer program. Refer to the Customer General Information section / Customer Invoice Info / Ahold Bill Payer Progam section for futher instructions..
Claim type Customer Check Request:
These are to replenish an the Bill Payer prepaid account and do not require validation. Note the claim ‘To request additional funds for the Bill Payer account’ and step as Trade / Other.
Preferred Partner Agreement deductions are to be stepped as Non-trade with a note stating to e-mail the invoice to the Regional Manager.
BUTTERBALL
Acosta is not the broker for Deli deductions for Butterball. Acosta is the “Meat” department broker only.
CAMPBELL’S
The customer signon must be changed to the customer signon that corresponds to the CI/contract, AHOLPH, GIANBW OR SSAHNE. Header note is required when changing the customer signon:
CAMPBL, PLUMO, PEPPFF (RAOS FROZEN/MA FROZEN)
AHOLPH header note CUST:1000007560
GIANBW header note CUST:1000009099
SSAHNE header note CUST:1000009207
PEPPBK, PEPPGR
AHOLPH header note CUST:0000013775
GIANBW header note CUST:0000013758
SSAHNE header note CUST:0000060103
If a claim comes in under client sign-on PEPPFF or CAMPBL when the products on the invoice are RAOS Dry, RAOS Frozen, or MA Frozen and the customer sign-on is FOODLNE but it is for Ahold (AHOLPH, GIANBW, SSAHNE) Acosta is not the broker, but the claim needs to be transferred to Ahold so the other broker has visibility. Step the claim to Unknown – Transfer to Another Branch – Closed and add these notes to the line: “TRANSFER TO PAYER # 1000007560” and add the identifier from the SOP and “NOT ACOSTA” to the check field.
If a claim comes in under PEPPGR when the products on the invoice are PF Frozen and the customer sign-on is FOODLNE but it is for Ahold (AHOLPH, GIANBW, SSAHNE), it will need to be transferred as Acosta is not the broker. Step the claim Unknown – Transfer to Another Branch – Closed and add the line note: “RECODE to D26-PZ04 on payer # 1000007560.”
If a claim is Fairshare (retail merchandising) and a division is not given on the invoice transfer/use cust # 1000009207 - SSAHNE (Stop & Shop).
Due to Ahold’s 10 day turnaround time for all bills, for Campbell’s signon CAMPBL POP/price point verification is not required. Also, if the customer invoice is missing detail, that is not required either. The Ahold team will supply this, as requested, for things such as CSA, PWC Audit, etc.
If contracts for NE/NY contain differing amounts, use the contract that supports the billing, if they are the same one contract can be used for validation.
If a customer invoice does not specify the division and the “All Locations” contract cannot be found, any division contract may be used as long as the AUSA contract number matches the invoice.
For Redemption Overlays: These invoices will be for a lump sum amount and it will reflect just one Ahold division. The invoice will also reflect wording such as Buy/Get, Gas, Must Buy, CSM (not an all-inclusive list).
The estimate contract is entered in Acoustic DemandTec and subsequently fed to the ACOSTA Relay system, creating a Virtual Promotion Folder that houses a copy of the estimate contract
Campbell’s Ahold team receives an email from Ahold with the final amount and this is forwarded to the BMA
The BMA will index the Ahold email into ACOSTA Relay system in Backup Documentation as an email with the AUSA contract number reflected in the customer reference field
Acosta will use the Estimate contract and attach the Ahold email showing the actuals as the contract to validate the invoice from Ahold and make the payment within the payment terms. The email will match the amount of the claim.
Shopper Marketing deductions do require contract, Mars Job #, and proof of performance.
If the contract states ‘KEY WEB MESSAGE’ or ‘DIGITAL AMP PACKAGE’ for an Ecommerce Deal, it is considered Shoppers Marketing.
Freetown and Stop & Shop customer invoices are considered non-trade.
If they create as Customer Check Request step to Closed.
If they create as ATB send to Campbells to handle internally.
Pepperidge Farm Stuffing claims must be split between Giant Foods Landover & Stop & Shop. The contract that supports these claims is the Stop & Shop contract. Step the claim to the sales team to request the breakdown between Giant Foods Landover and Stop & Shop.
If more than one client event # supports the customer invoice use the client event # that contains the last billed date on the customer invoice.
If the date that is being billed crosses over two different events, select the event that has more days covered. For instance if bill is for 4/30-5/7 and events are through 5/2 and starting 5/3 there are 3 days in first event and 4 in second event, the 2nd event would be selected.
When Ahold repays, they combine many repayments into one, and the customer reference is VARIOUS. The GCIT will request the support for the repay from Brigitte Mountz – brigitte.mountz@retailbusinessservices.com. Once received, the repay must be split out in SAP by individual invoice number, then applied to open deductions or cleared to trade events. GCC should step VARIOUS claims Ready to Clear – CCA with the note, “Please split in SAP.” When new claims are created, GCC will work those as normal.
Advantage billing is stepped as Trade – Other. No contract or POP is required. Client is providing the event breakdown.
Non-Trade claims for Freetown and Stop & Shop: Customer invoices are considered non-trade. If they create as a customer check request, step to Closed. If they create as an ATB, send to Campbell’s to handle internally.
If the invoice total matches the redemption amount on the contract, then the claim can be processed.
For all Ahold divisions, Vendor Code 040240 indicates that the invoice is for RAOS/MICANSO. Please follow the directions above if the claim needs to be transferred and review the Campbell’s SOP for Not Acosta Listing.
2% Ecommerce deductions should follow the normal process for Shopper Marketing. See below invoice:
Cargill
Ahold is no longer a Billpayer Customer and will be deducting moving forward.
For Ahold, Markdowns are handled internally by client.
CHATTEM/SANOFI
For Sanofi Markdown/Disc invoices and contracts: these are considered non-trade and should not be marked as reset. No client event number is required, per client.
Ecom claims will need the detailed backup. These claims will need to be split by brand and division. Cleared to Trade – Other to an event that will be provided by Sales.
Pre-paid invoices for ECOM 2% billings should be deducted are are not to be paid out of the pre-paid account. Claim type: Customer Invoice should be closed. Claim type: ATB should be worked. ATB claims will need to be split by brand and division, and cleared as Trade – Other. Event number is required. Customer Invoice claims should be closed as Unknown – Unknown with a note saying that the customer will deduct.
CHICKEN OF THE SEA
Advantage Billing deductions are cleared to an event. These should be stepped as Trade – Other – CRA Request Event #. These will need to be split by UPC that are listed on the Purchase Orders.
POP is not required
Retail Merchandising Program / Fairshare is a fee charged to support the customers retail initiatives.
Non-Trade / Retail Merchandising Program.
COCA COLA NORTH AMERICA CCNA
Advantage Program – These should be ATB claims only, not check requests.
Event numbers provided on the contract are by division/location and should be assigned based on the invoice.
Listing of 2024 Advantage Event Numbers:
Locations:
Stop & Shop – Manchester & Freetown
Giant Food – Jessup
Giant Company – Carlisle
CCNA is no longer on the Bill Payer program.
Funding #s are located at the bottom of the customer invoice and will determine the customer sign-on (refer to the Customer Invoice Info section for the customer sign-on).
ADUSA Stop & Shop – FND-NP4025
ADUSA Giant Foods (Giant Landover) – FND-GF4025
ADUSA The Giant Company (Giant Carlisle) – FND-GM4025
ATB (deductions taken via C&S.)
VIP/Billback Contract – VIP = Competitive Retail in AHOLD stores –
VIP is an allowance the client gives AHOLD for items being pulled through C&S during the promotional period, usually the entire year, but can be contracted quarterly, bi-annually, or annually. This gives AHOLD a competitive retail price.
Scan Types:
BILLPAYER
Use the bill splitter Excel files below to assist in breaking down claims.
Index as DBW.
1st file (Coca Cola Bill Splitter 5.5.18) is used if the following categories are on the same contract:
BO/Simply Ades 52oz, CO/Simply Punches 52oz, AA/Simply Lt Ades, E4/Minute Maid Lt Ades 52oz, BX/Honest Kids 8 pk, LV/Honest Kids 59 oz, V5/Honest Kids 8 pk box.
2nd file (Coca Cola Bill Splitter 9.17.19) contains Fairlife Milk 52 oz.
3rd file (Coca Cola Bill Splitter 01.20.20) All units invoiced for V5 are a different scan rate from the other two brand codes BX & LV, those have the same scan rate.
Bill splitter does not contain brand codes RN 59 oz Smoothie or RW 59oz 100% Juice. Instead use 90% of RN and 10% on RW.
Example of Customer Invoice for DBW example on next pageExample of Customer Invoice for DBW example on next page
In this example, the total amount will be split out to the various products within the product group, providing an amount for both the ‘direct’ business and the ‘indirect’ business as there are different event numbers for direct versus indirect. This would require a claim line for each of the amounts we see = 8 claim lines. Each claim line would be coded as Trade – Scan.In this example, the total amount will be split out to the various products within the product group, providing an amount for both the ‘direct’ business and the ‘indirect’ business as there are different event numbers for direct versus indirect. This would require a claim line for each of the amounts we see = 8 claim lines. Each claim line would be coded as Trade – Scan.To get the case total, divide the claim amount ($19,588.60 by the offered rate on the contract ($1.20) = 16,324 cases.When you place that number in this field (enter with no comma), it will calculate the rate for you into this column.To get the case total, divide the claim amount ($19,588.60 by the offered rate on the contract ($1.20) = 16,324 cases.When you place that number in this field (enter with no comma), it will calculate the rate for you into this column.Use this column when a customer invoice is billing for Direct and Indirect. - GC and GLUse this column when a customer invoice is billing for Direct and Indirect. - GC and GLUse this column when a customer invoice total is billing for indirect divisions SSNE and/or SSNY and GLUse this column when a customer invoice total is billing for indirect divisions SSNE and/or SSNY and GLUse this column when a customer invoice total is billing for all divisions - GC, GL, and SSNE & SSNYUse this column when a customer invoice total is billing for all divisions - GC, GL, and SSNE & SSNY
When the customer deducts individually as a direct (only) or indirect (only) account for product grouping:
Fill in the dollar amount for the brand along with the cases for that same brand.
To calculate the cases, take the total units found on the invoice and divide by the case pack (Ex: 262,572 total units divided by 6 = 43,762.
The case rate will automatically calculate for you once these two entries have been made.
Confirm the case rate with what was offered on the contract.
The contract unit costs will need to be cross referenced against the unit costs found on the customer invoice in order to create the DBW with the category breakdown
When the dollar amount is filled out, it will divide the amount up amongst the various products within that grouping.When the dollar amount is filled out, it will divide the amount up amongst the various products within that grouping.
Manual calculations must be added. The case rate and the quantity must be figured out by user and added. See below.
Invoices ending in CSM only - approved to clear to brand mis-match - event will be only for Brand 09.
ECommerce Claims:
No contracts required
No POP required
Events are lump sum.
Claims Breakdown:
ECommerce Event Numbers:
For duplicate claims only:
GCC/CRA add the product and the banner in the notes.
2026 Advantage Billing file:
DOLE:
Acosta no longer handles Ahold for Dole.
EAGLE FAMILY FOODS
Advantage Billings and ECommerce are handled as Trade. However, there are no contracts. Trade – Other.
Please see below for 2025 Client Event Number listing for Ecommerce and Advantage Billings
EDGEWELL
Edgewell does not submit a separate claim for the fee C&S charges (cust ref # ending in an F) for deducting on behalf of Ahold. They add the fee amount to the claim causing the claim $ amount in the header to not match the customer invoice amount. If the claim header $ amount does not match the customer invoice amount, refer to the C&S check remit to see if the difference is the fee.
If the AUSA code # on the customer invoice is listed on the attached Excel file the product is private label and not handled by Acosta. Refer to the Edgewell SOP for private label note requirement.
Email private lable check requests to janet.coleman@edgewell.com and attach the email to the claim.
Edgewell is tracking the spend for C&S fees by category. Money needs to be allocated to the event by category. Follow the fee section in the C&S SOP to determine the invoices being billed for, then break out the fees by category percentage on the invoice.
Ecom 2% invoices are cleared to Trade. No contract or POP required. Event should be requested from Sales. The DBW will be created based on the Wet Shave PPG provided in the event.
FILLED BAGEL:
Fill Bagel is on the Bill Payer program. Refer to the Customer General Information section / Customer Invoice Info / Ahold Bill Payer Progam section for futher instructions.
All trade and non-trade deductions are claimed from the Bill Payer funds available. Each month an FBI/BPO team member will create a ‘check request’ for each deduction listed on an Ahold monthly statement provided to FBI/BPO. The ‘check request’ will create a claim in GenWeb and should be validated. No check will be issued and a check request form is not required. Valid claims can be closed referencing ‘PREPAID’ in the check number field.
The FBI/BPO group should be notified via BagelfulsAR@Acosta.com of any invalid claims.
GA PRODUCTIONS:
Ahold is a prepay customer for GAPROD. This is part of the transition into the new TPM system with associated claims integration.
HARVEST HILL and SUNNY D:
APPLIES TO CLAIMS PRIOR TO 5/20/2023 - When a claim has been identified as Stop & Shop, the customer reference # in AR needs to be updated with “SS” followed by a space, in front of the invoice number. In TPM, the market can not be changed to Stop & Shop. Instead, “SS” plus a space will be added in front of the reference number. (Ex. SS A539694). A copy of the invoice should not be attached in TPM for Stop & Shop.
Advantage Program event numbers:
2024 Advantage Agreement Promo ID
Effective May 20, 2023, Acosta is the broker for Stop & Shop.
Event numbers for clearing 2% Ecom claims:
2024 Ecommerce Agreement (2% fee)
J&J SNACK
Any claims received with a client claim date (MEI Issue Date) after the transition date 1/1/2025 but are for performance "pre-transition" should be returned to the J&J Snack team to include the note "Pre-Transition Performance", capture the date of the activity, the brand, and a brief description of what the customer is claiming.  This must be notated within their proprietary system.
There are no check remittances or cover sheets for J&J Snack prepay accounts. The funds are taken from the accounts by the customer.
Ecomm 2% events:
J.M Smucker
Invoices that include the wording ADVANTAGE SHORTFALL or SWELL SHORTFALL it does not mean it is a shortage. It is for LDI/Spoils.
For E commerce 2% tax invoices - pull the client order invoice from the Patch. Specific COI or date range depending on ADUSA banner. On the event detail report – you will need to find events with a PV commitment type. Ecommerce 2% event can also be located by searching in Promo Name (Column K) of the Event Detail Report. There should be one event/PPG per SBU – Consumer (JIF), Coffee, Pet, and SBS.
Preferred vendor is considered PV tactic types.
For claims with a performance period after FY25 a maximum of $1000 overspend per PPG per promotion with no additional support needed.
VIP ADUSA deal number will not pull on the SBA planner tabs. You can confirm it's a VIP when it pulls to the VIP tab or has a long deal date timeframe.
VIP will use an EDLP tactic type on the event detail report.
Typically, will have VIP in promo name column (column K).
For Shipper VIP's, (will not have VIP is promo name column) the event will be under Pallet-Display Tactic type - the event is named after the item.
For Seasonal VIP's, you have to look under both EDLP and Pallet-Display Tactic Type.
For Scan and Ad deductions, search AUSA# in Ahold Planners attached on Sharepoint site.
When pulling POP for Scan deductions, pull IRI data 3 days before and after promotions start and end date.
For Ahold Pet and SMS, search for AUSA# in Promotion Contract ID (Column H) of the event detail report to find event to clear deduction to.
When searching in the Event Detail Report, if there is a discrepancy between the invoice rates and the event rates, but all other elements of the promotion match – deal dates, products, deal ID, tactic type – continue validation process for DBW and POP and add notes indicating the discrepancy then step to CRA to resolve.
PPA reports by sign-on are to be run using the below customer names:
AHOLPH – The Giant Company or Giant Carlisle uses Giant Martins from the PPA report.
SSAHNE – Stop n Shop uses Stop n Shop from the PPA report.
GIANBW – Giant Foods or Giant Landover uses Giant Foods from the PPA report.
Portal job aid:
KENS:
Slotting: Slotting deductions can use a spin report for POP if item cannot be found on a memo tracking report.
2oz, 64oz and 128oz product is considered Food Service.
Ahold spin report:
Spin reports should only contain products that are on the invoice.
If the spin report is reporting less than needed for validation, check the spin on the prior week claim to determine if they billed for less than what is on the spin. If so, as long as the extra cases from the prior week are within 10 cases or less of the case shortage from the current week, the claim can be cleared. Note the current claim with the amount of cases short in the spin and that the difference is from the prior week overage and provide the claim number, reference number, and number of available extra cases from the week before..
Indexing the spin: In the customer reference # field enter the Customer Reference # of the claim and the week ending date of the spin, EX: M799456 06/06/2020.
Ahold Lumper Fees are considered non-trade.
2025 ADUSA eCommerce 2% fees are cleared to event 26L-112-064A. There is no contract or POP required.
If events are closed, Ken’s regional manager has approved the use of the next quarter’s events.
Advantage Billing: Detailed backup is required for validation. Attach contract titled “Supply Chain Preferred Program Agreement” in AR. Use event # 26L-112-062A.

REPAY INFORMATION SECTION
Customer Invoice Issues – Disputing BBs, Double Billing, etc.
These cases are filed through the AP Portal. Once determined these are their invoices, AP team will research and pull the file together and they will assign a Case # and close the file and then send to the AR team to respond on their created invoices. We will not get an email back with the solution. Only way to check on these if approved, is to check the AP payments on the Check Remittance for a positive amount. We can open dialogue once AP indicates they have closed the Case and assigned a Case # and sent to AR. Follow up can be done by contacting the AR group and AP group with the Case # to get a status via email address  rbs.solutions@retailbusinessservices.com. If you do not get a response after two or more weeks, let your Supervisor know so that we can get assistance from our Sales Team.
Client Invoice Issues
Once repays are approved, submit your request through the AP Portal. AP will research and we should have a Case # in 3 Business Days via email from the portal. Once we have the Case # we should allow a week for them to respond in the AP Portal. If we do not get an answer after a week, we can start the communication via email or phone to get a status update. It is suggested we follow up with email and then phone. If you don’t hear back, please get with your Supervisor to follow up with Sales. We should not let these go beyond 30 days without follow up.
Email for AP rbs.solutions@retailbusinessservices.com
Phone # 717-960-1700 Option 3
Repay Process:
From the status of Repay Letter Sent, re-use the follow up step codes. If customer has not responded re-use the repay follow up step code and follow up with customer. Attach follow up emails to the claim.

Invalid Repay Process:

Only 15 invoices per case can be submitted. If attaching support documentation, the total file size cannot exceed 5MB.
A case ID number will be emailed to the PRS from the portal within one business day. Note the case ID number in the claim. Follow the invalid claims process and check the repay’s process via the portal via the case ID number.

sections.title: CUSTOMER GENERAL INFORMATION
sections.content:
Customer Invoice Info:
Is line level detail indexed on the customer’s documentation (customer invoice, customer check request, unsaleable/spoils, post audit, EDI 812/820) or client deduction notice if one of these documents is included?  YES
For the Brookshire Grocery Customer, the Customer Invoice and Contract will be same for many of their deductions (claims where they have to bill the Client back for monies offered – Billbacks – Ads – Slotting).                                                              The Customer Invoice will be searched under Back UP Documentation and the Customer Contract will be available under Event Scheduler.  There will be no dollar amount available to use in the Search Screen since we are using the Customer Contract as the Customer Invoice as well.
If an invoice says ‘pricing error’ it could be for many things – list cost pricing, promotional allowances or freight discrepancies.
All promotional deduction invoices reference the customer’s SAP portal processed check stub.  The number in the first column is an internal number which is unnecessary to a CRA.  Be sure to look at the check stub to make sure the invoice number on the claim is correct.
We do not receive actual customer invoices for billback claims, lump sum ads, slotting, missed deals or price protection.  The processed (accepted/approved) SAP documents serve as invoices for these types of deductions.
With the exception of billback claims, all of these will be in the form of lump sums.
It will be necessary to back into billback claims.
Divide the amount deducted by the billback rate on the SAP deal sheet to determine the number of cases being billed.
Fair Share (retail merchandising) invoices may have a pre of “FS”.
Po related/Invoice Reduction Notifications (IRN) for payment differences is mailed to the client the same day and the customer will not provide additional backup.
Price changes require 60 days notice and approval per document:
Contract Info:
Using the date ranges found on the Customer Invoice will help to narrow down the Event Scheduler search results.
The “Deal Number” can sometimes be used in the Customer Event # field of the Search Screen to aid in finding the Customer Contract.  NOTE: The Deal Number is not always loaded into this field by the sales team, so if the Customer Contract is not found by using this number in the Customer Event # field, you will need to refine the search.
All contracts are done in the customer’s web SAP portal, and when accepted, the processed SAP deal is sent to the BMA to link to the VPF.
All deals are contracted to this customer in ORDER DATES.
POP Info:
The validity dates on the customer’s processed SAP document are the order dates for the promotion, so sales analysis reports can be based on these dates.
Ads may be found in Feature Vision.
Other General Info:
If Brookshire Grocery acknowledges that a repay is due to the client, the invoice will show this repayment.  The repay line will have to be split from the valid claim amount, however, this line will be closed with a note stating that Brookshire Grocery repaid on the same check as the deduction.  No repay letter is needed.  The check remit must be attached to the claim as proof the amount was repaid.

Delhaize Deduction Code: The Deduction Code file helps to find out the Deduction Types on the Customer Invoice.
Delhaize Check Remittance Codes: The check remit may have enough information to validate with and a customer invoice will not be needed.
01 MLP claim variance
02 freight allowance claim variance
06 qty claim variance -OS&D (overages, shortages, damages, case pk)
24 Off invoice (OI) allowance variance claim
L7/L8 discount variance claim or any other miscellaneous adjustment
ZZ customer generated invoice claims
Payment made via EFT, not live check, “Allowance followed by UPC” 02 in the EDI format is an off invoice.
Hannaford invoices will have an “H” before the customer (vendor) number and Food Lion invoices will have a “W” before the customer (vendor) number. The check remit will identify the division for each invoice.
The MV prefix indicates the MVP Program for Food Lion and Delhaize which you must use the FOODLNE signon.
Partial Deduction:
If the customer invoice total does not match the claim header, refer to the Split Claims Job Aid.
The check remit can assist in determing if the claim is a partial deduction. If the customer invoice ends a B,C,D, E,etc that indicates it is a partial deduction.
Cancelled item invoices are for product that were refused and sent back to the manufacturer by the customer.
Pricing and OI Post-Audits: All Post-Audits for Pricing and OIs need to be submitted to Sales for review. Delhaize’s policy is to start the 90-day requirement on price changes to begin when it’s submitted to Category, not when it’s loaded in Cost & Deals. Once stepped to the BMA, the BMA will send to the BM and ask that they supply backup on whether or not the Post-Audit is valid.
CMA Fee: Monthly fee/calculation that Acosta pays each month for endcap shelf space. Claims team will work with the Sales team for the detail and approval letter.
Cash Discount:  Delhaize does NOT provide a Customer Invoice for Cash Discount claims, but will provide a tolerance variance or header level discount adjustment for the cash discount on their PO related claims invoices.
Contract Information:
WOW is an 8-9 week promo that gives a brand more tactics than just price reduction, display, etc…A WOW contract must be reviewed to determine the allowance type (ex. Scan).
Contracts will be entered under FOODLNE and HANMNE. All previously existing contracts will be found under DELHANE (for post audits before 2017). These 3 sign on’s will be used to find contracts in ACOSTA Relay.
Contracts will include multiple promotional periods and allowances. When validating a claim, look for the promotional period that matches the dates loaded in the VPF. Also, the naming convention of the contract will include the promotion start date, which indicates the dates that the contract is for.
The naming convention in the promotions screen will include the start date of the promotion for contract.  The naming convention in the promotions screen will include the start date of the promotion for contract.
Other General Info:
Claims that create as customer check request for Delhaize sign-on (DELHZMST), will be 3rd party check requests.  A header note will be entered with details stating the check is for a 3rd party customer and the payee name will be listed as to who to make the check out to. The customer sign-on for the claim will be change to reflect the division (FOODLNE or HANMNE).
Beginning April 2, 2023, ADUSA companies will implement a 2% COGs fee on ecommerce sales.
Products sold via Instacart, private brand products, all non-UPC fresh products, all fresh produce, and alcohol are excluded.
There is a $2500 threshold for deductions, meaning if a vendor’s e-commerce sales don’t total up to $2500 or above for a given week, no deduction will be taken.
The charge will be taken as a weekly deduction from purchase orders.
There will be no contract, as this is policy.
Claims will need to be stepped to Sales for an event number.

REPAY INFORMATION SECTION
Customer Invoice Issues – Disputing BBs, Double Billing, etc.
These cases are filed through the AP Portal.  Once determined these are their invoices, AP team will research and pull the file together and they will assign a Case # and close the file and then send to the AR team to respond on their created invoices.  We will not get an email back with the solution.  Only way to check on these if approved, is to check the AP payments on the Check Remittance for a positive amount.  We can open dialogue once AP indicates they have closed the Case and assigned a Case # and sent to AR.   Follow up can be done by contacting the AR group and AP group with the Case # to get a status via email address VMOSupport@adusa.com.  If you do not get a response after two or more weeks, let your Supervisor know so that we can get assistance from our Sales Team.
Client Invoice Issues
Once repays are approved, submit your request through the AP Portal.  AP will research and we should have a Case # in 3 Business Days via email from the portal.  Once we have the Case # we should allow a week for them to respond in the AP Portal.  If we do not get an answer after a week, we can start the communication via email or phone to get a status update.  It is suggested we follow up with email and then phone.  If you don’t hear back, please get with your Supervisor to follow up with Sales.  We should not let these go beyond 30 days without follow up.
Email for AP  VMOSupport@adusa.com
Phone # 717-960-1700 Option 3
Food Lion/Delhaize

sections.title: CUSTOMER GENERAL INFORMATION
sections.content:
Customer Invoice Info:
Is line level detail indexed on the customer’s documentation (customer invoice, customer check request, unsaleable/spoils, post audit, EDI 812/820 or client deduction notice if one of these documents is included)?  YES
Red Media and Supplier Relations are the same. The lump sum on the contract is for the entire year.
Hy-Vee customer invoices often show comments that reference “week ending”, followed by a date.  When searching for the contract, the date shown as “week ending” has to be in the same week the contract ends.  For example:
The contract can end any day between 6/17/2013 and 6/23/2013.
Claim reason Special Price:  Hy-Vee invoices show a reason code of Special Price on many different types of claims, including billback, count/recount, slotting, display, WOW Buy or E-Buy offers.  Review the contract to determine what the claim is actually for.
Customer invoice number:  Many Hy-Vee customer invoice numbers begin with BILLBACK.  However, this does not necessarily mean the claim is for a billback.  It could also be a count/recount.
Fuel Saver claims:  Hy-Vee always bases Fuel Saver claims on 20 gallons.  The claim amount will be 20 times the contract rate.  Example:  The customer invoice states FS [product] 0.40; the contract states Fuel Saver Cents Off: $0.02, with a comment of SRP of $5.99 w/.02 Fuel Saver.
Customer Invoice:
Contract:
Fiscal Month customer invoices:
Rather than creating a customer invoice with a specific date range, Hy-Vee may submit bills showing Fiscal Month <month> <year>.
While their fiscal year starts in October, Hy-Vee’s fiscal months align with calendar months.  In this example, they are billing for June 1, 2019 – June 30, 2019.  Check the comment section of the customer invoice, as they may specify a smaller time frame (e.g. week ending 6/16/2019) within the fiscal month.
Attached are the codes Hy-Vee uses on their check remits.
Contract Info:
Once a contract has been submitted to Hy-Vee, there is no way to revise it if anything changes (usually it is that the dates are extended, but could also be that product is added, the rate changes, etc.).  If a contract is found but the detail on the customer invoice does not match, check the VPF Plan Notes and/or Plan or Event Attachments for documentation supporting a deal revision.
E-Buy:  Hy-Vee contracts that show E-Buy Offer Form are to be treated as a count/recount.  E-Buy contracts do not show a deal amount.  They show a regular Store Case Price and a Special Store Cost.  The difference between the two is the E-Buy offer amount.  In this example, the deal amount is $21.38 per case.  ($51.38 regular price - $30.00 special cost = $21.38)
Hy-Vee customer invoices and contracts often reference “term” when referring to their billing periods.  This verbiage may be in the Reference Title, or may be in the Comments section.
Hy-Vee terms are four months each and are defined as January – April (1st term), May – August (2nd term) and September – December (3rd term).
Ad Offers, Store Pre-Orders and Future Deals contracts will now be pulled for Pending, Approved and Finalized statuses, see examples of Pending status below.
Other General Info:
Hy-Vee has two warehouse divisions – Chariton, Iowa and Cherokee, Iowa.  There will usually be a deduction for each division.  The deductions do not always occur at the same time, but most offers are made to both Chariton and Cherokee.
Hy-Vee requires a minimum of 60 day notification for pending price increases (see attached policy).

sections.content:
BARILLA
Hy-Vee admin fees are split to a separate line, coded as Trade – Other, and stepped Ready to Clear-CCA.  The event info for these is blue box tactic YR08.
Hy-Vee receives a swell allowance from Barilla.  Claims for spoils/unsaleables are considered invalid.

Pacific Foods claims for Lomar Distrbutiong update the customer # in the header to CUST:1000009354.
A claim for Temp Trip Device is considered a freight violation charge.  Step the claim as Non-Trade/Freight and note “send to deduction team for recode”.
While Hy-Vee does not subscribe to Nielsen, they do subscribe to IRI.  A weekly file containing info on all Campbell’s brands is loaded in ACOSTA Relay that is to be used to validate POP and price point per client SOP.  Search for POP:Movement/TPR using CAMPMST/RPTCUST.
Repositrak fees are considered non-trade unacceptable spends.
Claims for cross dock fees are coded Non-Trade/Freight and sent on the closed claim feed with the note: Crossdock fees.

Repositrak fees are cleared to an event.  Search for the contract/event in AR using %repositrak% in the Event Description.
COCA COLA
Supplier Relations Partnership Fees are paid as a check request for CCNA.
HyVee is allowed a seven (7) day date shift.
DOLE
Admin Fees will be split to a separate line, coded as Trade / Other, and cleared to the same promotional event.
The customer invoice number on a hard copy Dole invoice will not show the F2.
Repositrak fees are cleared to a Client Event #.
EDGEWELL
Red Media is a lump sum event cleared as Trade – Other. DBW is created based off event and PPG provided by Sales.
HARVEST HILL
Harvest Hill will accept Hy-Vee deductions for missed OI on cut/shorted product if the claim is under $1000.  If the claim is over $1000, it must be discussed with the RSM and SVP for potential repay.
J M SMUCKER
PO related claim deductions will always have a cash discount amount that is not on the invoice remittance.
Directions for working and researching PO-related claims:
Deduction amount minus the backup amount will be considered CASH DISCOUNT (validated by JMS DRS).
Shortages and overages will be netted and the amount sent to JMS DRS to resolve if results in a deduction amount (shortage is more that overage) – if overage is higher than shortage, see below additional direction to manage.
Remaining amount (e.g. list cost, off invoice, etc.) will be deemed PROMOTION/TRADE and researched/validated by Acosta CRA.
If the OSD portion results in an OA over our $100 threshold, once the shortage portion is resolved, the remaining amount will be transferred to Acosta to manage as PROMOTION/TRADE.
Deduction will need to be split in HR per normal rules.
If GCC is unable to locate invoice in Relay, the GCC will look for invoice remittance (not the check remittance – but a customer invoice type) in AR.
If located and does not match the claim header amount- factor in the cash discount – 2% of the PO total, there will be no backup for the cash discount portion.
If no backup is located, then check for cash discount via the Patch Report.
If the claim header is more than the cash discount, backup will then need to be requested from Hy-Vee.
Invoices with “Deduct Shortage” are OI allowances on shorted product and are to be cleared to a penalty fee.
Proof of Performance issues with FHS and Coffee items are approved to clear without Sales approval.
For claims with invoices beginning with a “1” – IRI data will likely be insufficient. Client has approved these claims for clearing with insufficient POP.
When searching for claims in HR, search by the customer reference number (external number) with an asterisk at the end. This will show if there are multiple records for the same reference number.
KING ARTHUR FLOUR
When a deduction comes in with a customer reference # ****Short Pay, the customer invoice number will not match the claim header.  These deductions need to be escalated for customer invoice.  The CRA will need to contact sales to determine which Hy-Vee invoice makes up the short pay.
KIKKOMAN
Kikkoman does not participate in the ReposiTrak program.  Non-participating clients are billed quarterly.  In addition to the customer invoice, attach the Hy-Vee ReposiTrak letter and step the claim Non-Trade/Service Fee, Awaiting Processing by CCA.
MARS WRIGLEY CONFECTIONARY US
Damages/Unsaleables are cleared to the below client event #s.
CORE CE #1001P0003FMN239D
KIND CE # 1001P0003FMJ239D
NESTLE COFFEE PARTNERS
Nestle Coffee participates in the Supplier Relations program.
For Hy-Vee Starbucks that Acosta handles, the vendor #000371.
For Hy-Vee PDI Starbucks that Acosta does not clear, the Vendor #006997 – PDI.
For any other - Acosta doesn't handle any ready to drink items. These are handled by Nestle.
Starbuck Quarterly Swell are considered trade and cleared with an event/contract. Code as Trade/Other and clear to event.
NEWELL
Claims for WOW Buy are coded as Trade-Other.  A WOW Buy is a discount that is provided at 20% or higher to the customer and their stores.
Product ships to the stores beginning on the dates on the forms. Once products have been shipped to the stores, they bill. Therefore, the week ending date of the invoice will exceed 7 days compared to the contract date.
Markdowns do not require a contract.

Settlement Netting Information :
Kroger uses Settlement Netting to offset funds due to Kroger from suppliers against payments due to vendors. See below document for details.
As shown in the above document, payment data will need  be exported from Supplier Connect by the client to create the individual deductions taken by Kroger for Acosta to then validate.
Customer Invoice Info:
Is line level detail indexed on the customer’s documentation (customer invoice, customer check request, unsaleable/spoils, post audit, EDI 812/820) or client deduction notice if one of these documents is included?  YES

Use the Master Client Sign On.
If the invoice can not be found in Acosta Relay using the Kroger sign-on(s), try HARRCN.
Kroger invoices download once a week on Thursdays.  The GCC will search for the customer invoice on calendar day 5 and if not available, hold the claim and check again on calendar day 9.  If the customer invoice is still not available by calendar day 9, the GCC will step the claim Escalate – Cust Inv Not Found.
Kroger invoice (s) with the format (Ex. 092-A420066-438) are in repository available by searching Back Up documents. Using the wild card key (%) before and after type in the last 3 digits of the invoice number in the customer reference number field and search. Using the date of the attached invoice, the remaining invoices can be found to equal the claim amount.

The attached documents outline the 2025 KOMPASS billing model.

Kroger Deduction Code: The Deduction Code file helps to find out the Deduction Types on the Customer Invoice.  NOTE: Disregard the Peyton warehouse codes.  Peyton now follows the Kroger Food codes.
Note – the deduction code ‘08’ for net total dollar difference could be for any PO-related issue.  All PO-related
issues including pricing, missed OI, etc. must be researched for possible causes.  Refer to the PO-Related
Claims, Pricing Deductions, and Cash Discount job aids for more info.  Examples of reason code 08 are included
in section 26, however, these are just examples and are not all-inclusive of every way to work an 08 claim.
Sometimes, Kroger will provide multiple codes on one line item (see below for example).  Refer to example #s 4 &
5 under Pricing for an example on how these types of claims will be handled.  The exact process will vary based

If this occurs, the claim total will be less than the invoice total and there will be claims in Acosta Relay with the same customer reference number creating a duplicate error.  Refer to the Split Claim Job Aid on how to proceed.  Sometimes, Kroger will reflect the split amounts on the CI itself:

If the first 3 digits of the invoice begin with 092, 181, or 060, the last 3 digits are typically the division number (KMA) that Kroger is billing for.  Otherwise, the first 3 digits are the division/KMA for non-PO related promotional invoices.
If the division code in the customer invoice # doesn’t match the division code listed in the invoice description, for the below format invoice, use the division code in the invoice description to determine the correct customer sign-on. PO-related claims – If the division # on the customer invoice is not correct, use the division in on the PO/COI itself to confirm the correct division for the claim.
PO-related claims – When the customer invoice total doesn’t match the claim total for a PO-related claim, review the Client Order Invoice to determine the cash discount amount.  To determine the cash discount, divide the Terms Discount by the Gross Total.  This will show the cash discount percentage.  If the claim amount and the invoice amount are off by the same percentage, then the difference is due to cash discount.
In the below example, $490.01 ÷ $24,500.64 = 2 so the cash discount is 2%.

And the invoice total was $236:
$236 x 2% = $4.72 which is the difference between $236 & $231.28.  The difference in the invoice &
claim is off by the amount of the cash discount.
NOTE: If a non-pricing item is included on the claim, such as freight, the cash discount will not be taken on the non-pricing item.
Ocado is a virtual store that Kroger uses which are automated fulfilment centers for some delivery and pickup orders. To recognize is a claim is for Ocado, the reference number begins with the word DEAL and in the below format:
The invoice must be reviewed to determine the Division number to identify the KMA and signon to search for the contract.
The deals for Ocado are offers that Kroger copies from DemandTec and they are not in AR with the contract number on the invoice. The contract will need to be located using products and dates. The quick reference signon chart at the top of this document contains a column for Ocado.  The above inovice shows Orlando as the store name. Locate Orlando in the Ocado column and the Gen Web Claim Sigon column can be used as the customer code to locate the contract.
The contract allowance will be In cases, but Ocado Invoices are In units.
Deductions that have prefix of DMQ (Debit Memo Quantity) are for Unit Shortages/Damages. Signed POD only indicates that the delivery has been made on specific date/location. All final payments are subjected to count at the point of decant, after driver departure. See below policy document.
Deductions that have prefix of DMC followed by original invoice number are list cost deductions.
Kroger claims are billed on a weekly basis with a Saturday week-ending date.  On the invoices the week ending date will be listed above the Billing Period.  Kroger’s billing cut-off is noon on Saturday.  The dates being billed for are the Sunday thru noon on Saturday of the week identified by the week-ending date, as long as those dates are within the contract. For example, on a division with ad dates that run Wednesday-Tuesday, a promotion with dates 8/11-8/24 will have an invoice for week ending 8/14 that is billing for 8/11-8/14 (8/14 until noon), an invoice for week ending 8/21 for 8/15-8/21 (8/21 until noon, plus any post-noon billings from 8/14), and an invoice for week ending 8/28 for 8/22-8/24 (plus any post-noon billings from 8/21).
If there are back to back promotions and the Acoustic deal # is not available, refer to the billing period listed underneath the week-ending date to confirm which contract the claim is billing for.
Due to the way the contracts are being entered into Kroger’s system, you may see a variance between the allowance offered and the amount Kroger is taking on their deductions.  If a case rate does not divide out evenly to the number of units in a case, the allowance will reflect extended decimal places, causing a slight difference.  Extended decimals will only show when math is verified, because the contract and invoice rates will match.
If a contract is offered for a $3.45 KATS allowance on a case of 16, the allowance works out to $.215625 per unit which will cause a rounding issue when converted to cases.
When Kroger bills, they will reflect the extended amount based on a “unit” rate instead of a case rate.  However the bill will reflect the correct case rate for the contract.
To determine if there is a case rate vs. a unit rate discrepancy, divide the extended total by the quantity on the bill.  If you get an uneven amount (in this example $3.45766129) then this is a rounding issue.
$857.50 ÷ 248 = 3.45766129
There are instances when, due to rounding, Kroger will deduct for less than the contract rate.  Ex: the contract shows a case rate of $2.48 for a 24pk item.  The unit rate is $.10333.  Multiplied by 24, that comes to $2.4799/case.  Instead of rounding up to $2.48, Kroger will sometimes cut off the number and claim only $2.47.  If this occurs, the claim can still be validated, even though the contract rate is showing a higher rate than the invoice.
Arizona Select Distributing is a distributor that Kroger may purchase through.  The Kroger invoice will reflect Arizona as the vendor and the deduction will be taken on an Arizona check.  If Arizona submits a claim, the invoice itself may be for multiple vendors.  If the claim total is less than the CI total, review the detail to determine what portion is for the actual client.
Jake’s Finer Foods (JAKEHO) may purchase through Kroger.  If the Kroger invoice references Jakes Finer Foods, the contract must also reference Jake’s.  It will appear that Jake’s is being referred to as the client, but the product being billed for and contracted for will be for an actual client.  The contracts will still be loaded under the correct Kroger division based on the division identified on the invoice.

If an Offer # (Acoustic DemandTec #) isn’t listed at the bottom of the invoice to search for a contract, there may be a contract # referenced in the explanation section of the invoice.  Contract #s starting with S are Ralph’s contracts and can be used to find contracts the same way the Acoustic DemandTec #s are used.  If the invoice is lacking sufficient detail to validate and no other instructions are provided in the SOP for that type of invoice, try searching for the contract to see if it provides sufficient information to validate.
Some Kroger invoices may drop the the leading digit of the contract number, normally a 2, from the DemandTec contract number. The invoice may state 504456, but the actual DemandTec contact number would be 2504456.
If an invoice includes multiple divisions, the claim header sign-on should remain KROMCI, the Kroger Master sign-on. DBW lines will need to be updated to reflect the divisional sign-ons.
OSA on the invoice indicates deduction is On-Shelf Availability. Validated as Retail Merchandising.
Contract Info:
Kroger is an Acoustic DemandTec customer for certain allowances, refer to the customer invoice to see if an Acoustic # is provided.  Acoustic deal #s are 7 digits long.  If the # on the invoice is only 6 digits long, add a 2 to the beginning of the # when entering it in the Check Number field for Acoustic download issues.
Kroger also uses VCP (Vendor Collaboration Portal).  Deal #s that are 4 digits are for VCP contracts.  VCP contracts will list the case rate allowance as a unit rate.
Contracts for Fred Meyer warehouses 015 and 022 will share the same VPF under Kroger signon KROGPT.
For Food 4 Less claims , NoCal=C&S/798 and SoCal=F4L.  Food 4 Less contracts for division 704 that have comments “NoCal/SoCal only” are for both F4L and C&S (798).  F4L contracts for division 704 that have comments “798 FOODSCO” are for C&S only.  If neither the 704 nor the 708 box is checked and the comments state “Ralph’s” then the contract is for Ralph’s only.
Any F4L 704 off invoice contract submitted through Acoustic DemandTec will be converted to KATS for C&S warehouse 798.  Any KATS claims for 798 that show OI as the allowance type on the contract can be validated as a KATS.
Kroger may bill by inner packs on HBC clients.  Refer to the client matrix to identify whether the client you are working is an HBC client.  If they are then you may have bills referring to the inner pack rate, instead of the case or each rate.  The Authorized Product listing out of Acosta Relay can identify the inner pack size of a case.
Example:
Customer invoice reflects $6.00 Customer invoice reflects $6.00
Contract reflects $48.00 Contract reflects $48.00
Jake’s Finer Foods – refer to the customer invoice section for Jake’s Finer Foods information regarding contract and invoice.
If a claim is for Peyton and more than one contract for the appropriate KMA is available, link the contract that includes ‘P’ in the code as shown below:
When events are selected, do not just consider calendar dates.  Consider the Kroger billing dates.
Ex: The Kroger invoice shows it is billing for week ending 1/01/22 and two events are provided with the contract: one that ends on 12/31/21 and one that begins on 1/01/22.  The event ending 12/31/21 should be used to clear the claim as that is the event that actually covers the week the customer is billing for.  The billing for week ending 1/01/22 is billing for dates 12/26/21-1/01/22, but it is not the full billing for the date 1/01/22.  The event that ends on 12/31 covers the vast majority of what the customer is billing for.
A ‘roller’ is Kroger’s term for a price reduction tag (TPR).  “Pass through” rollers mean each division may have a difference price point.  “Hard-coded” rollers mean the same price point is requested across all divisions.  Example of a roller reference on a contract’s comments:
LTO (Limited Time offer) contracts are manually entered and are available under customer sign-on KROMCI.  The offers are for special pallets/displays that may consist of limited time product or regular open stock that is on a special pallet/display deal.  The invoice will not identify the claim as being for LTO items.  If a contract can’t be located under the appropriate division’s sign-on, try searching under KROMCI.  The contract comments will identify the claim as being for LTO.
POP Info:
Kroger job aid shows all warehouses that supply to each division.  When running sales summaries users can run it for all warehouses that support the division the invoice is for.
When running sales reports – Anytime warehouses 388,185,181,087 or 086 are listed on the customer invoice run the sales report for the correct division sign on and PEYTCI both.
For division 708, when pulling POP, the AR sign-on RALFFDB can be used, however, it must be pulled specific to ship to #s 553, 559, 788, 552, 789, 551, 561, 563, 558, 560, 1, & 565.
If Kroger orders a pallet or shipper of seasonal items, to clear out the remaining stock, a scan markdown contract may be offered for the items that Kroger still has in stock.  Because those items shipped in the pallet, there will be no POP for the individual case UPC on the invoice & contract.   If a sales analysis or shipment report is being used as POP, the report will have to be run using the pallet UPC.  If we don’t have a list of which items made up the shipper/pallet, then sales will have to provide that info.
Ruler division mostly orders displays/pallets.  Open stock contracts are created to clear out remaining product.  If a sales analysis is required as POP, use the pallet/display UPC.
When verifying POP quantity for HBC claims that are billed by inner pack, remember that sales reports show quantities in cases, so to validate this bill you would multiply the number of cases by the inner pack quantity to ensure enough was purchased to support the bill.
Example:
Customer invoice reflects $6.00 Customer invoice reflects $6.00
Contract reflects $48.00 Contract reflects $48.00
Authorized Product Listing shows that there are 8 – 3pks within a case.  $6.00 x 8 = $48.00 Authorized Product Listing shows that there are 8 – 3pks within a case.  $6.00 x 8 = $48.00
If price point verification is required for a claim and the division is Peyton, an ad can be pulled for any of the divisions that Peyton supports: Cincinnati, Columbus, Michigan, Indy (Central).
Other General Info:
Post audit and unsaleable claims from ATB upload clients will auto-route to the step Req CI From GCIT so the GCIT can check the appropriate portal for backup.

sections.title: BACKUP RETRIEVAL INFORMATION
sections.content:
GENERAL BACKUP RETRIEVAL INFORMATION
Is GCIT responsible for obtaining backup from the customer? Yes
If yes, is there a customer portal?  Yes
If yes, does GCIT request backup? Yes
Is check remittance information required to request backup? No
If backup is needed for a PO-related claim, note the claim “Please pull PO-related backup from Supplier Connect portal.”
If backup is needed for a Vitacost PO-related claim (COI identifies it as Vitacost, or PO# is 6 digits long starting with 37, or PO # is 9 digits long starting with 1000), note the claim “Please request Vitacost backup.”
If backup is needed for a DSD claim, note the claim “DSD backup needed.”
If backup is needed for Fred Meyer non-food, note the claim, “Please request Fred Meyer non-food detail.”
If backup is needed for CRV, note the claim “Please request CRV backup.”
If detail backup is needed for KOMPASS claims, note the claim “Please request KOMPASS detail.”
If additional detail is needed for claims with ref#s that contain A, F, G, or S, note the claim “Please request additional detail in the Supplier Connect portal.”  Additional notes are required to explain the issue with the backup already provided.  NOTE: Review the customer invoice “User Comments” section to determine if a specific email address has been provided to request the detail form.  If so, note the claim with this information.
Backup for manufacturer coupon claims (ref # format #########_######, C####### or CS#######) – Acosta is not responsible for manufacturer coupon claims and Kroger does not send us the backup for these types of claims.  If a client is requesting backup, have the BMA provide them with the email address where the backup can be requested from.
For JAYCIN claims, if invoice & claim total don’t match and info is needed to identify which invoice(s) the claim is for, note the claim “Please request which invoice(s) the claim is for.”
If detail is needed for fuel surcharge claims, not the claim, “Please request detail for fuel surcharge.”
Barilla
If not available in AR, request manufacturer coupon backup from GCIT.
Bush
If not available in AR, request manufacturer coupon backup from GCIT.
Eagle Family Foods
GCIT will request check remittances from Supplier Connect.
Mars Petscare US
Kroger Slotting claims (invoice 092-SXXXXX)
The detailed backup will need to be requested from Jacob Morton, Jacob.Morton@effem.com. It will not be provided in Supplier Connect or the Mars Compass system.
PO related claims GCIT will pull the customer invoice from the Kroger portals and will check Mars Petcare’s system Compass for any client order invoices for the invoices in a format similar to 0034159081 or 0034159081CM.
Method
Pos are listed on an Excel spreadsheet which is requested from Brian S. Hansen (BSHansen@scj.com). Copy Kroger AR Specialist Allie Ostrander (Aostran@scj.com) on the request email. This report aims to provide Sales better access to Kroger’s invoiced amounts and reduce requests for initial invoice information. Exception requests should still be expected for invoice copies (needed for pricing disputes), coding discrepancies (ex. Pack vs. Sleeve), or other exceptions. These requests should route to Allie Ostrander and additional questions can be escalated to Brittany Dimock (Bdimock@scj.com) or Brian S. Hansen.
Nestle Coffee
GCIT will pull all backup for Nestle. If unavailable in SAP and Supplier Connect, the CRA/GCC will step as Unknown/requesting backup and note the claim INCOMPLETE BACKUP or MISSING BACKUP. This will go over on the feed to Nestle alerting the team that the backup is not in SAP. Once deduction reopens, the CRA will step to the GCIT to re-pull from both portals.
Rosina
Backup for -R and -Z invoices (Panoptic) are requested from the client Pignaszak@rosina.com.

BUSH

TRI-UNION SEAFOODS – CHICKEN OF THE SEA

COCA COLA

EDGEWELL

JM SMUCKER COMPANY

For claims with a performance period after FY25, a maximum overspend of $1,000 per PPG per promotion is allowed, with no additional support needed.
Kroger Coupon claims for JM Smucker contain an Excel file with the invoice details. Refer to the instruction sheet and the JMS and Hostess Coupon templates for how to prepare the data for validation.

Kroger Supplier Connect and Panoptic Portal job aids:

Extra Scan Week/Additional
Most Kroger contracts require an extra seven days beyond the contracted dates (ie. If the contract is written 2/15/2026 – 2/22/2026, claims up to 3/1/2026 would be valid). This can be referred to as Exit Scan Week, Additional Scan Week, or Clean Up Week on any post-audit claims that are received.
There are two types of invalids for Extra Scan Weeks that are not received as post-audits:
ZDP: Any post-audits claiming for Additional Scan Week that reference ZDP are invalid. This extra scan week was not written into any contracts between Kroger and JMS prior to 2026 and are therefore invalid.
General Extra Scan Week post-audit: In the post-audit invoice, Kroger attaches a copy of the contract. Check the comment section on the contract. If there is a comment that says, “CM AGREED TO NO EXIT SCAN WEEK,” or similar, then the claim is invalid.

8.  Deduction Type:  Post Audit:
Internal/external auditors find claims that the customer is entitled to but did not take from previous years. Post Audits should be researched in the same manner as other claims by accessing previous year’s files.
NOTE:  The post audit claim must first be researched to ensure the customer has not already billed for the allowance before the normal validation process can begin.
Once the post audit claim has been researched to ensure the customer has not already billed for the allowance refer to the appropriate allowance section of the SOP to continue with validation.  If the post audit is for an allowance not defined in an allowance section of the SOP refer to the post audit example for validation information.
General Post Audit Info:
Customer Invoice:
Kroger will send pre-notifications for their post audit deductions.
Post audits with an H in the reference number are taken by Connolly Conusulting.  Connolly will deduct for all divisions on the invoice, but Kroger will deduct each division separately on the check remit.  This means the invoice amount will total more than the claim amount.  To match the claim amount, refer only to the section of the customer invoice that is for the division the claim is for.
If a post audit references previous claims that are all for Peyton and the contract involved is a Peyton contract (see Customer General Info section – customer invoice & contract sections for Peyton identification), then the post audit is also for Peyton.
Below is Kroger’s post audit guidelines-warehouse.
Below is Kroger’s post audit guidelines – DSD.
Kroger will sometimes include Dialog History (example below) from the Acoustic DemandTec submission with their post audit backup.  If this is included, review the dialog for any agreements sales made to changes to the deal.  If sales approved a change on the deal dialog,the change can be considered valid.
Below are Kroger’s requirements for new item introductory allowances.  If these are not met, Kroger will submit a post audit.  The post audit is submitted due to lack of an acceptable contract so after confirming that there was no offer meeting their requirments and a Kroger-acceptable allowance was not received, a post audit for this issue will require FCM approval to clear.
New Item Introductory Allowance:
New items must have an introductory allowance on them.  Exceptions to this would be items downsizing or pack changes.
If a New item is part of an existing RBP group, and those items have an existing contract on them, a contract will need to be entered on the new items only to match the existing contract(s) starting 4 weeks prior to the KOMPASS Period.
The allowance must be loaded through Trade point with the following guidelines:
EDLC performance type
OI (includes local DC, Peyton, and DSD)
15% minimum off list cost
Start 4 weeks before the start of the Kompass period and end the last week of the Kompass Period. (example, if the item is for a Period 5 Kompass update, the contract would need to start Week 1 of Period 4 through Week 4 of Period 5 (8 weeks).
You must work with your category manager to determine when the first promotions will occur on the items.
If a new item will be promoted (ad or display) within 4 weeks of it hitting shelves, the new item allowance must either be 15% off list cost or whatever the promotional allowance will be when on ad or display, WHICHEVER IS GREATER.  This includes items that are part of an existing group; the new item contract will start before the current items in the group.
Contract:
KPCs – Kroger assigns Kroger Product Codes (KPC) when they allocated product to support End Cap displays and these are sometimes referenced on post audit claims.  As long as the item used in the display/KPC is the same item on the contract, Kroger can claim the unit allowance.  Ex: An item ships in varying sized packs.  A contract is offered on 4pk cases, but the contract lists a unit allowance.  Kroger can claim the unit allowance on that same item that came in other pack size boxes if that product was used in the display.
These may not be referred to as KPC on the post audit invoice.  If Kroger lists product UPCs on their invoice that are not valid, they may be billing for a KPC.  Example CI & contract below. 8.1Customer Invoice for Post Audit, Example #15:
This is a post audit for a pallet/shipper/display that didn’t receive the equivalent allowance offered to open stock items.
Kroger’s policy is that all modules, displays, shippers, etc. are considered promotional buys and should receive at a minimum the same allowance offered on the same open stock item.  In this example, Kroger shows that the cost charged for a shipper UPC on two PO#s did not include a discount to bring the net unit cost (NUC) down to match the open stock NUC that was in effect at the time the orders were placed/shipped.They are saying they were charged $601.68 for the Apple Punch shippers UPC 00044 which have 184 bottles on them.  That makes the cost of the items in the shipper $3.27.  If you look up the shipper UPC in Product Definitions and refer to the Modular tab, you'll see it consists of open stock UPCs 00820 & 00824.During the same time as the POs the shipper shipped on, those two open stock items were included on an EDLC contract to receive a $7.52 OI.  The contract shows the regular UNIT cost of $3.27.  The pack size shows 8 bottles in a case so 8*$3.27 = $26.16/case (which can be confirmed as the correct cost in Production Definitions on the Pricing tab for those two UPCs).  $26.16-7.52 OI = $18.64/case.  $18.64/8 bottles in a case = a promotional net unit cost of $2.33.The $3.27 cost of the bottles in the shipper minus the $2.33 cost of the bottles shipped as open stock = $.94 cost difference where the shipper was charged more than the open stock.  $.94 x 184 bottles in the shipper = $172.96 they are due off the shipper to bring the cost down to match the open stock cost.  (Kroger showed this math by calculating the open stock cost of $2.33*184 bottles which comes to $428.72 and then they subtracted the $428.72 from the shipper cost of $601.68 to get a total of $172.96 per shipper.)To validate, review the COIs for the POs the shippers came in on.  PO 44842 shows $127.07 allowance and PO 45812 shows $74.60 allowance on the shippers.  That alone reduces the $172.96/shipper that Kroger is claiming so the entire claim is not going to be valid.  You’ll need to follow post audit validation requirements to determine if it’s just those allowances to account for or if there have been any other claims related to those CRA VALIDATION SPECIFIC
25.  Deduction Type: Retail Merchandising Program – KOMPASS Resets (Single Source)
PLEASE NOTE: The below process applies for all clients.  Client SOP instruction for how to
handle Retail Merchandising Program claims is followed AFTER the below process of obtaining detail and
stepping to sales to confirm what portion is Acosta’s responsibility happens.  The below process is not skipped
unless the client-specific section of this SOP states it is.
If detail is not available in AR, request it from GCIT.
Once Kroger provides the detail, step to sales with a note to please advise how much of the claim Acosta is responsible for. The BMA will work with the BM to confirm how much of the bill is Acosta’s responsibility and how much is the client’s or another broker’s.  The BMA will step the claim back to the CRA and either attach an email or forward an email to the CRA at that time.  The email will be from the BM to the client advising the client as to how much of the claim is Acosta’s responsibility.  If the BMA forwards the email to the CRA instead of linking it to the claim, the CRA must link the email to the claim.  The CRA will then code the claim and close it in Acosta Relay.
REPAYS
When Kroger deducts against an Acoustic DemandTec contract incorrectly, there will often be
multiple claims that are deemed invalid.  When sales receives a repay approval request for an Acoustic
related issue, the BMA will review DemandTec for all claims related to that repay that will also be deemed
invalid.  The initial repay letter will be Rejected and sales will provide a list of all claims affected.  The
PRS/CRA will then re-write the repay letter using the additional spreadsheet tab to list all related claims.  The
PRS/CRA will look for the remaining claims in Acosta Relay, link the same repay letter to all claims and step
them all for Awaiting Repay Approval at the same time.  If any claims that are not below the client’s
tolerance are not available in Acosta Relay yet, the PRS/CRA will provide the claim information to their
supervisor.  The supervisor will then work with the GCC team lead to have the GCC watch for the remaining claims and escalate them immediately for repay.  The PRS/CRA will then link the repay letter and step the remaining claims once they are available.  If any of the identified claims have already been cleared, the PRS/CRA will work with the CCA and/or client to reverse those claims in the client’s system and issue the repay.
Category manager and Director approval:  With the exception of repays for wrong vendor, all repays for invoices with ref#s that include -A, -C, -NC, -R (for pricing only), -S, and all numeric ref#s (typically client order invoice #s for PO-related deductions) require category manager approval before Kroger will repay them. Category Manager and Director approvals are required for List Cost and Off Invoice repay requests.
When the claim is stepped to Awaiting Repay Approval, enter ‘REQ CATMGR APRVL mm/dd/yy’ in the Check Number field.  The mm/dd/yy is the date the claim is being stepped to Awaiting Repay Approval.  Ex: REQ CATMGR APRVL 06/29/20.  NOTE: If an Acoustic deal # was in the Check Number field, overwrite it with this information.
