sections.title: CUSTOMER GENERAL INFORMATION
sections.content:
Customer Invoice Info:
Is line level detail indexed on the customer’s documentation (customer invoice, customer check request, unsalable/spoils, post audit, EDI 812/820 or client deduction notice if one of these documents is included)? Yes
A suffix of ‘SW’ at the end of an order invoice number on the check remit indicates that amount is for swell allowance.
K-VAT invoices beginning with a ‘PM’ prefix include an S or T in the Type column. The S represents spoils or scans and the T stands for tracking.
Items labeled with T are count/recount and must have a contract.
Items labeled with an S will not always have a contract because it may be for discontinued items. If no contract is located to support an item marked with an S, step as Contract Not Found.  If the BM/BMA provides a contract, the S is for a scan.  If a contract is not provided, the BM/BMA will provide a note that states the item has been discontinued.
If the customer invoice states Deleted/Discontinued for the respective UPC and the allowance is stated as a scan or a count/recount allowance, validate it as a markdown.
KVAT will sometimes split a customer invoice between multiple checks. If this occurs, the claim total will be less than the invoice total and there will be claims in ACOSTA Relay with the same customer reference number creating a duplicate error. Refer to the GCC Step Code Job Aid/Split Claim Job Aid on how to proceed.
Contract Info:
K-VAT contracts are loaded via Event Scheduler.  Use the unit and case UPC when searching for contracts, as either UPC can be on the contract.
Promotional Calendar:
Scan contracts start on Wednesday and end on Tuesday.
Tracking contracts run from Saturday to Saturday. This results in Wednesday, Thursday and Friday of contract start date being omitted on a tracking invoice, but is picked up on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday following the contract end date.  Tracking claims will end the Saturday following the end date of the contract and are valid based on customer promotional policy.
On the Contract:
Specification on the allowance rate fields:
Monthly / Roller Per Case Truck: Count/Recount (C/RC)
Monthly / Roller Per Case Scan: Scan
Per Unit Scan (Closeout):  Markdown
Rates can also be located in the Personalized Offers sections of the contract.
Ad requirements for promotions:
If a contract has the Weekly Ad, Monthly Ad or Special Ad boxes marked, an ad is required as part of performance per generic help.  An ad may also be mentioned in the comment section.
POP Info:
A Sales Summary from ACOSTA Relay is used to support K-VAT claims unless there are specific requirements in the client SOP for POP.  If the sales summary does not provide enough sales, IRI/Neilson can be used following client and generic help POP requirements.
Ads are located under ADCLIENT/MIDMKX in backup documentation.
Other General Info:
Close-out Policy
Failure Fee
If a new item fails to perform at a rate of 6 cases per week after being in the store for 9 months, a failure fee will be charged.
This is in addition to supporting
Closeout Program
A Close-Out is considered to be any item that is an overall Food City deletion or an item that is de-authorized from a planogram version (example – item is removed from an 8’ version, but remains in a 12’ version).
All remaining warehouse inventory must be picked up by the manufacturer.
All Close-Out items will be billed at 50% of cost on a scan basis.
Pick-up full cases at Food City Distribution Center .
Final clean up thru Reclaim.
DSD no failure fee.  Credit store at time of pick up.
NOTE: Sometimes K-VAT will order through the customer Merchants Distributors Incorporated (MDI). If this is the case, the claim may come over with the MERCCN customer sign-on; however, contracts will be found using MIDMKX sign on.  POP must be run at the direct customer level, using the MERCCN sign on.  Some clients that K-VAT purchases through MDI are:

Deduction Type: Bill Back
A Bill Back claim is a per case allowance offered for a specific performance requirement. A per case bill back allowance is claimed by the direct buying customer for product purchased from the client, or by the indirect customer for product purchased from the direct customer. This is an allowance the customer will bill the client for. This is not an automatic discount given off the face of the invoice.
Bill Back Billing Period
McLane bills Bill Back invoices weekly on Thursdays. The billing period is for the previous Thursday thru Wednesday. For example, if the Date of Charge on the customer invoice is 4/10/14, McLane is billing for 4/3/14 – 4/9/14.
When we present a new Bill Back promotion to McLane and there is an existing promotion with the same data (ie. Items, amount), McLane will extend the existing promotion already in their system. The Date of Change needs to be used when validating a claim against a contract. In the below example, the Date of Charge is 3/12/14. This means McLane is billing for 3/6/14 – 3/11/14. However, the Buy Dates are shown as 2/1/12 – 3/11/14. This means that this promotion has not changed in McLane’s system since 2012, only the promotion has been extended from year to year.
As long as the contract covers the billing period, it can be used to validate the customer invoice. In the example above, the billing period is 4/3/14 – 4/9/14. As long as the contract covers this date frame, it is not required for it to cover the Buy Date of 2/1/12 – 3/11/14 due to McLane extending contracts as described above.

There are 3 things to look at on a contract to make sure it is the correct contract for a claim: is it a national deal (all divsions), is it for one or more divsions, but not all of them (uncommon) or is the contract for a certain store/indirect of McLane for all divsions.

A per case off invoice allowance (OI) is given to the customer as an automatic discount for product purchased from the client. If the customer does not receive the allowance off the face of the invoice they will deduct for it. Deduction Type: Off Invoice
A per case off invoice allowance is given to the customer as an automatic discount for product purchased from the client. If the customer does not receive the allowance off the face of the invoice they will deduct for it. If the customer requested an allowance that is not valid, the CSC will send a notification to the customer in writing. Customers view purchase orders as contracts. If they are not notified of allowance discrepancies, they will pay according to their purchase order total.

Deduction Type: Bill Back
A Bill Back claim is a per case allowance offered for a specific performance requirement. A per case billback allowance is claimed by the direct buying customer for product purchased from the client, or by the indirect customer for product purchased from the direct customer. This is an allowance the customer will bill the client for. This is not an automatic discount given off the face of the invoice.
Customer invoices ending in ‘RP’ with verbiage of “Retail Pricing Billbacks” are billback deductions.
When working some non-food accounts for Off Invoice and Billback, the customer invoice allowance may not match the contract.  The allowance per case may be broken down into inner packs per case.
For example:  contract offer is for $12.00 per case. The claim comes in at $4.00 as the inner packs are 4/3 or 3/4 ($12 per case / 3 units per case = $4 x 3 inner packs = $12.00)

with a space before and after the letters.

BMAs are loading this in the Plan Attachments of VPFs.
Price Chopper and Rouses have a $6 admin fee.
Note: The $6 fee is not reflected on the AWG invoice – the invoice total and the claim total will differ by $6 – the difference is the fee.  When the claim includes the $6 fee, enter a clearing/math note on the claim or the DBW to explain the $6 difference. See the Alliance section for info about fees charged by Alliance for deduction.
AWG also charges a 15% fee (15% gain) for retail shipments  (Count/Recount/Warehouse Withdrawals).
There is a $200/item image fee penalty if an appropriate image is not provided when submitting new item forms.
Prior to 11/1/24, AWG charges a $510 Repositrak service fee (effective 11/1/24, the Repositrak service fee will be increased to $525)
Effective 11/7/25 Trace Gains is replacing ReposiTrak.  It is a mandatory annual fee for all vendors.  Please see below letter communication. Invoice example is in the Service Fee/Penalty section.

AWG charges a $100 Corporate Menu Labelling service fee for Deli/Bakery – invoice example is in the Service Fee/Penalty section.
A lot of AWG’s invoices may be very “generic” and not contain the details needed to validate the deduction.  Instead it will list different invoice #s in the body of the document.  If you see these invoices, you will search ACOSTA Relay for the other invoice number and most of the time, locate the additional details needed.
AWG will sometimes split a customer invoice between multiple checks.  If this occurs, the claim total will be less than the invoice total and there will be claims in ACOSTA Relay with the same customer reference number creating a duplicate error.  Refer to the GCC Step Code Job Aid/Split Claim job aid on how to proceed.

Always check the bottom left and bottom right of the contract for comments.  These sections will sometimes put limitations on the deal (ex: Scan good for week of ad only) or provide an additional allowance on top of the allowance listed on the contract.
When alerting sales for missing contracts on a deduction for indirects, always provide the indirect group/name that the contract is needed for, in addition to the standard alert information.
If the contract format matches the one below, it’s from Aptaris – which is AWG’s internal promotion system.  The Aptaris deal # is listed in the URL at the bottom of the page and the ‘child deal’ (indirect) # is listed at the top of the page.  If the customer invoice includes the Aptaris deal # or child deal # (often referred to on the invoice as ‘deal #’) it can’t be used to find the contract, but once the contract is found, the customer invoice deal # can be matched to the Aptaris #/child deal # in the contract to ensure the correct contract is linked.  If the invoice lists the child deal number, then the dash in the number as shown on the contract is replaced with a 0 on the customer invoice.

Other General Info:
At their discretion, AWG will charge $50 for backup and repay requests. Effective 7/1/24, the new rate of $60 will be charged for backup and repay requests (Invoice Surcharges).
AWG 60 days Lead Time for Price Increases are based off order date and not the vendor ship date.
For example, if the price increase is effective with a ship date on 7/3/23, we would back it up and communicate a 6/26/23 order date and that is when the 60 days is calculated.

sections.title: INDIRECT INFO
sections.content:
For help finding alternate signons for AWG’s indirect groups and the store names that typically run the ads within that group see the AWG ACOSTA Relay Cheat Sheet located in ACOSTA Relay under customer SOPs.
AWG indirects often convert their indirect BB into a scan.  Divide the BB rate by the case pack and if it matches what the customer is claiming, the claim can be validated.  Note: Converting a scan to a BB is not authorized unless the comments of the contract specifically allow for it.  The client/customer manager & BMA are not authorized to approve this an exception.
When the indirect converts a BB to a scan, use scan POP to validate the claim and use Scan as the reason code on the claim line.
For check requests claims - even if the check request was not indexed with the email showing sales sent it to be indexed, if the contract to support the indirect check request is not available in ACOSTA Relay, the claim can be validated using the contract included in the check request packet.  NOTE: If the check request is indexed without the sender’s email address, this is considered an indexing error and should be logged.
It’s possible for each indirect group to be offered two (or more) ads during the same contract period.  When this happens, there will be two contracts that appear to be identical.  The Even Description will identify one contact as AD1 and the other as AD2.
The attached list identifies if an indirect submits check requests or if AWG deducts on their behalf.
Alliance info:
Alliance charges a $6 fee on all grocery, dairy & frozen invoices.
Alliance is an indirect group of AWG’s, made up of multiple stores.  With the exception of slotting claims and Deduction Request Process claims (see below), when working a claim for Alliance, use the ZZALDVKC contract.  For slotting claims, refer to the AWG_ ACOSTA Relay Cheat Sheet/Slotting Sheet tab to identify if the store Alliance is billing for has its own contract for slotting only (identified as ‘slotting only’).  If it does, that store’s contract must be used for slotting claims.  All stores not listed with their own slotting contract will use the Alliance contract.
See example under Billbacks to see an example of an Alliance BB claim.
The same ad can be used to support the claims for all Alliance divisions.
Deduction Request Process:
Alliance will submit deductions on behalf of the indirects listed below in lieu of those indirects being paid via check request.  The indirects will still submit check requests, but claims will not create in ACOSTA Relay.  A report will be extracted each week of newly submitted check requests, and the sales team will submit the report information to Alliance.  Alliance will create one deduction per client per week for submitted check requests.  Examples of the Alliance invoice with instruction on how locate the check requests the deductions are for are included in the various allowance type sections.
The customers involved (for both AWG & VMC) are:
Ball’s (ZZBALLKC/ZZBLLDKC)
B&R (ZZBRSUKC/ZZBRRDKC)
Cosentino’s (ZZCOSEKC/ZZCRODKC)
Harp’s (ZZHRPSKC/ZZHARDKC)
Harter House(ZZHARTKC) (AWG only)
Homeland HAC (ZZHMLDKC)
McKeever’s (ZZMCKEKC/ZZMCKDKC)
Pyramid Foods (Ramey’s) (ZZRAMEKC/ZZRAMDKC)
Queen’s (ZZQUEEKC/ZZQUEDKC)
Town & Country Salem (ZZTCSAKC/ZZTCSDKC)
Alliance will charge a $6/invoice fee and AWG charge an additional $6 for processing the deduction.  The $6/invoice will typically reflect as a Processing Fee and the $6 from AWG will typically reflect as a Deduction Fee.
For promotional dates prior to February 2021: For non-lump sum claims, one contract (ZZGOLDKC) will be used to validate claims for the Deduction Request Process.  After February 2021: For non-lump sum claims, one contract (ZZALDVKC) will be used to validate claims for the Deduction Request Process. The individual indirect contracts will still exist and can be used if the rate the customer is billing for differs from the rate on the contract.  Lump sums will still require the individual indirects’ contracts.
Ball’s:
Ball’s includes Hen House & some Price Chopper stores.  TPR fees for Ball’s stores will be deducted by Alliance on an Alliance invoice.  Use the Ball’s contracts to validate them.  Any other lump sums for Hen House stores are deducted by Alliance on an Alliance invoice and use the Ball’s contracts to validate them.  Any other lump sums for Price Chopper stores – see Price Chopper section.  All other allowance types will be submitted on a Ball’s check request form and deducted through the Alliance Deduction Request process (see last note).
Ball’s/Four B will charge a 1% late fee on any unpaid check request balances over 90 days old.  This will be a monthly recurring fee at the end of each month.
Unless the client is excluded from the Deduction Request Process, check requests should not create for this customer.
B&R:
B&R is part of the Deduction Request Process.
Unless the client is excluded from the Deduction Request Process, check requests should not create for this customer.
Caputo’s:
For BB & scan claims deducted on AM invoices, use Great Lakes Ad Group contracts to validate if the ZZGOLDKC contract cannot be used.
Effective 7/20/21 Caputo’s check requests for ads will no longer create claims.  AWG will deduct on behalf of Caputo’s and the invoice will provide the last 5 digits of the Caputo’s reference#.  Use the wildcard & search under both Customer Invoice & Customer Check Request to locate the Caputo’s detail.  ZZCAPUCH contract is used for the Ad fees.
Cosentino’s:
Cosentino’s is part of the Deduction Request Process.
Unless the client is excluded from the Deduction Request Process, check requests should not create for this customer.  Cosentino’s will charge a 1% late fee on any unpaid check request balances over 90 days old.  This will be a monthly recurring fee at the end of each month.
For promotional dates prior to 8/17/20, if “Group 100” is referenced in the description, the claim is for KC In House Ad Group (ZZKCADKC).  If “Group 100” is not referenced, refer to the Price Chopper section of this SOP.
Crest:
Crest can be a direct customer (CREFKC) or an indirect (ZZCRESKC).
If the claim is PO-related they will not issue a customer invoice.  The client order invoice must be found in ACOSTA Relay by using the customer reference number as the client invoice number.  (The customer’s PO copy is considered their backup).
Crest does not run any ads.  If a Crest invoice and/or contract shows ad money, it’s really for a display.
Any check requests 90 days or older at the end of Crest’s fiscal quarters will be deducted through AWG or VMC.  Crest’s fiscal year begins Oct 30.
Crest can accept partial check requests.
Crest will use their PO copy as their deduction invoice.  Their PO# is used as the customer reference #.  To calculate the claim deduction amount, multiply the Invoice Deduct by the Quantity Ordered.
Great Lakes Ad Groups:
For promotional dates prior to 8/17/20, Great Lakes Ad Groups all use the ZZADGLKC contract.  Ad & TPR money
will be listed on Ad Group 1.  After 8/17/20, the sign-on ZZGOLDKC is used for contracts & ads.
Gulf Coast 3:
For promotional dates prior to 8/17/20, this customer is part of Gulf Coast division’s Power Plus 2 (ZZP1GCKC). After
8/17/20, the sign-on ZZGOLDKC is used for contracts & ads.
Harp’s:
Harp’s is part of the Deduction Request Process.
Unless the client is excluded from the Deduction Request Process, check requests should not create for this customer.
Harter House:
Harter House is part of the Deduction Request Process.
Unless the client is excluded from the Deduction Request Process, check requests should not create for this customer.
Heartland:
If Heartland bills for a lump sum that shows as a TPR/Billback, it is really for an ad fee. Heartland does not have TPR lump sums.
For BB & Scan claims on AM invoices, for promotional dates prior to 8/17/20, use KC In House Ad Group, Great
Lakes Ad Group, or Nebraska Ad Group contracts (depending on which Heartland division is being billed) to validate
the claim if the ZZGOLDKC contract cannot be used. After 8/17/20, the sign-on ZZHEARKC is used for contracts &
ads.
Homeland (HAC):
Homeland is a part of the Alliance group, Alliance deducts for them through AWG, and charges a $6 fee for each invoice.
Contracts need to be searched for under customer sign-on ASSDKC with Division ZZALDVKC, as long as the contract does not say HOMELAND under the excluded on the bottom of the contract use ZZALDVKC to clear with. If contract cannot be found under ZZALDVKC division sign-on look for ZZHMLDKC.
KC In House Ad Group:
For promotional dates prior to 8/17/20, when AWG bills, they may reference groups K100 & K300 on the detail backup.  Case or unit-based allowances are handled the same, but the lump sum allowances will be listed separately on the contract by the K#.  For POP purposes, use the below list for which stores are part of each K group.  An ad for any store in the group is sufficient as POP for ad lump sums.
K100 = Sunfresh, Country Mart, Moser’s, Bings

sections.title: BPS Team Information
sections.content:
CRA VALIDATION SPECIFIC
Shortage/Damage –
When the customer invoice states shortage/damage the BOL is required to confirm if the claim is for shortage or damage if we validate non-trade claims for the client.  If we don’t validate non-trade claims, the claim will be stepped to the CCA without the BOL and either reason code Shortages or Damages can be used.
Repays –
AWG requires repay requests be a minimum of $50.  Also, they will not accept repay requests for order dates older than 36 months.  Repays are submitted via the online portal.  The portal can be referred to as AWG Connect, AWG Vendor Relations Request System, or Service Now.  See imbedded document for instructions on how to submit in the portal.  The portal is accessed by going to www.awgconnect.com and following the instructions in the attached job aid or by going straight https://awg.service-now.com/.  Please note, the username for the two systems is different.  Your login credential for Service Now is initially the same as for AWG Connect, but you will be required to change it when you first login.
Repays must be submitted individually – multiple claims cannot be grouped together into one repay letter.
Repays for Price Chopper, Alliance (including when Allian submits deductions on behalf of other indirects), and Rouse claims are submitted by the customer manager and not AWG’s portal. Refer to the Master Claims Roster tab of the AWG and Acosta Relay Cheat Sheet document to identify the customer manager for Price Chopper, Alliance, and Rouse.  When the repay is due for follow up, contact the BMA via email for a status update.
Repays for AM invoices are submitted in the portal, note the claim with the case#, and send the case# to the
BMA via email.  Follow up is handled by the customer manager.
NOTE: Instructions are to enter a 4-digit or 6-digit vendor # with preceding zeros.  The vendor # must always total 7 digits.  Add however many zeros are needed to reach 7.
Once the repay is submitted, the portal will provide a case number.  Enter the case # on the claim as it is required when following up with AWG for repay status.  When the claim is due for follow up, after confirming it hasn’t been repaid yet, access the portal and select Request Case Status.
Any repay that is rejected by AWG will result in a $50 fee to the client.
When AWG responds to a repay request, an email is generated by their system.  If more information is needed, the email can be replied to and it will deliver to a person.
Invalid Check Requests -
For the following indirect customers, send any invalid check requests to the Customer Manager listed, do not send them directly to the customer.
B&R – Kevin Bride
Ball’s –Grant Ellison
Cosentino’s - Grant Ellison
Harp’s –Frank Martin
Harter House – Tim Kinser
Homeland(HAC)/United – Richard Nelson & Jamie Crow
McKeevers –Grant Ellison
Pyramid (Ramey’s) – Tim Kinser
Queen’s Price Chopper – Grant Ellison
Town & Country Salem – Jay Morris
Wood’s – Tim Kinser
CRA Client Specifics
BUSH
If the regional manager provides approval to clear an invalid claim, they are cleared to the following events.
TA22101259 – AWG-Deductions Require Bush Sales Approval-For Invalid Audits
TA22101260 – AWG-Deductions Require Bush Sales Approval-For Invalid Fees, Etc.
CAMPBELL’S
PCE bills will need clearing instructions from sales and then approval from client finance to clear.
DOLE
Invalid claims for allowances on short product are not submitted to AWG.  Once the repay has been approved, the claim is closed with the WO settlement code.
GEORGIA PACIFIC
Step Merch Agreement claims to sales.  The BMA will provide a breakdown & commits.
A credit report is received once a month (no later than the 2nd week of the month) from the BM/BMA that identifies the cases AWG shipped to Rouse for the previous month.  If the report does not include UPC, description, allowance amount & credit amount for each UPC – return the report to the sales team and request the missing information. Run a Memo Tracking report for the Gulf Coast division (ASGCKC) for the UPCs on the report for the month the report covers plus the two previous months (total 3 months).
Use the memo tracking report & the credit report to identify which PO(s) and quantities are needed to account for the cases shipped to Rouse.  (More than one PO may be needed to account for the credit quantity of a UPC.)  Locate the claims for the corresponding POs (these can be found by searching for the corresponding contracts and looking in the VPF – claims would be stepped Awaiting Clearing Partial or by searching for the claims in ACOSTA Relay using the wild card and the client order invoice# as the customer ref #).  When determining which POs/quantities are used, check the previous months billings (other tabs on the shipment report) to confirm those same POs/quantities weren’t already used.
Once the claims for the POs are identified, confirm the claim was for billback allowance and was validated correctly.  Also confirm the rate deducted matches the rate on the credit report.  Remove the credit case quantities from the line they are on and add them to a new line.  Update the DBW to reflect this change and add a clearing/math note to the adjusted lines that the adjustment was made due to the ‘Rouse Exclusion for the month of ____.”  On the newly created line, enter a math/clearing note: Send to the client to handle Rouse exclusion internally.  No contract is required for the newly created line. Add to the shipment credit report the Acosta claim # and line # the credit was taken from, the commit #, client ref #, customer ref #, and UPC. Link the report to the newly created line for the credit portion.
If the same PO is being used for credit cases for a different month, create a new line for each month.
Once all adjustments are made, step all claim lines back to the CCA with a header note that the claim can now be cleared.
Once the adjustments for the month’s report are complete, search for any remaining claims for ASGCKC in Awaiting Clearing Partial that are for the month the credit report covered.  Any claims not used for credit adjustments can now be re-stepped to the CCA with a header note that they can now be cleared.
HOSTESS/ JM Smucker
Claims beginning with the pre-fix “PC” do not go to AWG’s portal for repay. They go to a third-party group, who verifies everything with David Underhill. PC##### dis-allows should be communicated to accounting@argretailers.com.
HOSTESS Vendor # 0007140.
JM Smucker Vendor # 0004329.
CCA CLEARING INFORMATION SPECIFIC
Crest –
Indirect check requests are always mailed to the corporate address PO Box 7510, Edmonton, OK 73083, not the store address listed on the check request.
CCA Client Specific
BARILLA
All event and funding issues are sent to the regional manager in lieu of alerting sales.
Claims for Crest & Homeland sauce EDLP allowances (Crest $.27 & Homeland $.25) are cleared under YR19.
Price Chopper & Alliance admin fees are cleared to YR12.
BUSH
• If the CCA needs funds, b/c they can do this in the client system for the client to approve, we will use
the Pending Update – Req Client step which is owned by the CCA and has a 7 day follow up.
• If at the 7 day follow up, the CCA still has not gotten funding approval, we will step the claim to
Request Additional Funds-Action Required, and seek BM assistance through appropriate notes on the
claim line for actions we have already taken and need their help with to get the funding issue resolved.
CAMPBELL’S
All events are fixed tactics.  Case/unit rates can be cleared to lump sums.
Deal loss recovery claims can be cleared to events that are off by more than the standard 30 day allowance.
Rouse check requests – enter the claim line amount from AR in the Paid Amount under Event/Tactic in e4 and ensure Planned Spend is reflected under Allocation Metric.  Click the Allocate button.  The paid amount under Funds does not need to be manually updated.
DAIRY FARMERS OF AMERICA
Deal Loss Recovery claims will follow the DFA overspend process.
Split claims and deductions for the Alliance deduction request process can only be partially cleared if:
All the events in the same division are ready to be cleared.
The line(s) not being cleared is invalid.
80% of the claim is ready to clear.
When partial clearing, detailed notes must be entered into the client’s system to connect each split
claim.
GEORGIA PACIFIC
AWG can bill 7 days prior & 7 days after the contract dates.  iPlan events are loaded to accommodate this already.  Ex: a 5week contract will be loaded for 7 weeks in iPlan.
ASGCKC claims are stepped Awaiting Partial Clearing unless they have a note from the CRA stating they can be cleared.
Preferred Vendor Agreement (PVA) claims are sent to Sherry Williamson, shrwilli@gapac.com.
HARVEST HILL
For Crest check requests submitted from a PO – add INV to the invoice number in TPM.
JM Smucker
All HB prefix invoices should be cleared to a markdown tactic type in CAS.
NESTLE NUTRITION
Merch agreements are sent to staci.checkan@us.nestle.com and CC the business manager.  The subject line of the email must include the client ref #, dollar amount, and “clear internally.”  The body of the email must explain that the claim is for a merch agreement and is to be handled internally by Nestle.
SUNNY DELIGHT
Indirect check requests for case or unit rate allowances can be cleared to lump sum events.
For Crest check requests submitted from a PO – add INV to the invoice number in TPM.

sections.content:
Customer Invoice Info:
Is line level detail indexed on the customers documentation (customer invoice, customer check request, unsalable/spoils, post audit, EDI 812/820 or client deduction notice if one of these documents is included)? No
Certco invoices are often included with the check remittance.  If the invoice included with the check remittance does not have sufficient info or is missing pages, check for the invoice under doc type 2-Customer Invoice.
Woodman’s PO is considered the invoice for Woodman’s PO related claims, and the claim is “backed into.” If the PO is not available under Orders/Invoices/PO, search for it under Backup Documentation Doc Type 2-Customer Invoice.  NOTE: The customer ref# is typically the client order invoice so the COI may need to be attached first so that the PO# needed can be pulled from the COI.
Woodman’s charges a $50 fee for scan re-prints (backup requests).
When Certco deducts for Woodman's invoices, the invoices will no longer be combined as one packet in AR. The validator will need to identify the Woodman's invoice #(s) listed on the Certco backup and link the Woodman's invoice(s) to the claim separately.
Customer Contract Information
If invoice is for a scan, contracts can be located in Event Scheduler under both: CERMMW and WOODMW.
Other General Info:
Certco cash discount policy is to take the discount on the gross dollar amount not net pay amount.
Certco cost change policy is to provide a minimum of 90 days prior to the effective order date.

sections.content:
Customer Invoice Info:
Is line level detail indexed on the customers documentation (customer invoice, customer check request, unsalable/spoils, post audit, EDI 812/820 or client deduction notice if one of these documents is included)? YES
The customer sign-on needs to be updated based on the Core-Mark division. Refer to the Excel document above (Core-Mark Acosta Team Div Responsibility). This will ensure the alerts are going to the correct business manager.
The Division number is the first two numbers at the beginning of an invoice.
Locate the division number on the Div Responsibilty file in column B. Change the customer sign-on the sign-on provided in column C.
The division can also be located on the check remit if available.
Core-Mark invoices with the letters FMI in the invoice numbers – this means FOCUSED MARKETING INITIATIVE and will be from Core-Mark Corporate and thus entered under COREMST.
When no Performance date is listed on page 1 of the customer invoice review additional backup provided to see if the performance date is available.  The customer will supply a receiving report or client order invoice with their deduction b/up to show what was received and what was invoiced incorrectly (then deducted by the customer).  It will be noted on the copy.
When customer reference/check remit has prefix MKT at the beginning the invoice will not reflect this prefix.
Contract Info:
NorCal and SoCal contracts can be found under Event Schedular and/or under Backup Documentation - Doc Type 17.

The Core-mark purchasing policy can be used for SLOTTING claims as approved by Campbell's Finance.  Policy is indexed under CAMPBL / COREPT (dco type 17) with customer reference of Coremark Policies.
C-store Quarterly Rebate Checks:
C-Store Client Development Manager will receive quarterly Envision Report from Campbell’s Finance via email.  Envision Report will provide event breakdown by product group and will act as DBW.
Envision report will be forwarded to Sales Team, who will request a matching invoice from the customer.  Invoice will be indexed as CUSTOMER CHECK REQUEST to create a claim in Acosta Relay.  GCC will break claim lines out and apply the C-store Event Number from the Campbell’s SOP.  Contract will be found under Backup Documentation, Doc -17 Contract, and linked to each line. Create DBW

TATA

POP is not required as long as the deduction is able to be matched up with a promotion (If rates, dates (within a week before or after) and items match).
Exception (PET & SBS only)- If the total units or total amount of deduction is significantly different, then reach out to sales to verify and request POP (bump chart).
Client approved to clear deduction despite if the units or $ amount are higher/lower. Their system will adjust accordingly once deductions are cleared.

2.Deduction Type: Scan
An allowance for products scanned at the store through the register and is usually billed in eaches, not cases. The customer should not be referencing a purchase order on a scan allowance.
A Scan invoice for SEG/Winn Dixie will have an added 5% scan service charge. The entire invoice including the service charge needs to be validated for the claim to be cleared.
The Service Fees shown on the customer invoice show they are calculated at 5%, however, this 5% is an ‘average’ amount and can vary up or down depending on each individual store involved. Because of this process, we need to change the method of how we load the Service Fee amount on the DBW.
Service Fees are applied to each of the Distribution Centers listed within the customer’s invoice. We will need to add up the fees for each Distribution Center shown and then calculate what ‘average’ percent will need to be loaded in the Admin Fee % column on the DBW.
To do this, add all Service Fees together, then divide that amount by the total promotional amount from the “Scan” DBW. If we use the customer invoice in Example #3 below, our calculations would be:
All Service Fees added together = $1,346.08. Total Scan amount for all items = $27,010.64. $1,346.08 divided by $27,010.64 = .0498351. Move the decimal over two spaces to get a percent of 4.98351. If we load this number in the Admin Fee % column on our input screen, the Service Fee will apply to each category involved. Because of rounding issues, we will most likely be a few pennies off the actual Service Fee total added from the customer’s invoice. That small difference should be added or subtracted from the category with the highest promotional volume on the category report.

When reviewing a C&S Customer Invoice number Invoice # or the check remit, if the Invoice number begins with 1, 2 or 3 and contains 9 digits, this is a C&S deduction invoice number the last 3 digits represent the buyer code The C&S Buyer Code Listing is used as a reference tool to identify which market area is responsible for the claim/deduction.
The Buyer number List can be accessed in Acosta Relay main screen under Claims then SOP Documents and should be used to confirm which division or indirect the customer invoice is referencing, although not all indirects are listed on this job aid.
On the Buyer Number List, column B or C, all West Coast buyer numbers are identified as ‘West Coast’. All other buyer numbers belong to East Coast (if buyer number identifies as Metro use CSWMNE, all others are part of Northeast  CSWHNE)
If C&S deducts on behalf of an indirect, the customer sign-on should be changed to that of the indirect. See Client or Customer SOP for Client specific exceptions.
If there is a difference between the last 3 digits of the customer invoice number and the buyer number on that same invoice, go by the buyer number. Example, invoice ends in 227 and buyer number is 647. 647 is the number to use with the C&S Buyer Number List for identification.
The majority of the C&S invoices will start with “CLA” moving forward, the buyer list was updated to reflect one tab.
CLA invoices will typically have a three digit buyer number included at the end however if the buyer number begins with a “0” the “0” will be dropped off from the invoice number.  For example if the buyer number is 052 the CLA invoice will only include the CLA the invoice number and 52.
The CLA invoices will include an Owner field which will sometimes include a buyer number.  If the buyer number listed here is different than the buyer number from the invoice number, the buyer number from the owner field should be considered.
If the CLA invoice doesn’t have a performance date but it has a contract number, the dates on the contract are the date to use to validate the claim.
If the CLA invoice doesn’t have a contract # or performance date then the claim needs to be step to the Sales team.
If the buyer number on the customer invoice is not found on the C&S Buyer Number List, please notify Bob Fallavolita at Bfallavollita@acosta.com in order to have the discrepancy investigated.
Buyer # 497 connects to a national merchandiser. This number connects to sixteen facilities across the country.

If 5% of that claim is the amount of the fee or more, the entire fee can be validated/cleared considering only the highest dollar claim.
If the 5% of the highest dollar claim is not the amount of the fee or more, calculate 5% of the highest dollar claim and that amount of the fee claim is cleared against the one claim.  Continue following this process moving to the next highest dollar claim, etc.
For example, there is a $1000 fee.  The highest claim amount associated with that fee is $15,309.45.  5% of $15,309.45 is $765.47.  $765.47 of the $1000 claim will be cleared against the contract(s) of the $15,309.45 claim.  The next highest dollar claim is $8000.  5% of $8000 is $400 which is more than is needed to complete the $1000 claim so the remaining balance of the $1000 claim will be cleared against the contract(s) for the $8000 claim.

2. Deduction Type: P-Vendor (P&D Pass and Deduct) Billing
C&S is a direct customer and buys from the client. The C&S indirect customers "bill back" to C&S their OIs, BBs, Scans, as these indirects cannot deduct from the client.
P-Vendor deductions are deals set up at C&S for specific indirect customers. Instead of setting up the deal as a billback at the retail customer level, or an OI at C&S, the deal is set up as a P-Vendor deal. It is similar to an OI, except it is for a specific indirect customer for a specific time frame. The indirect customer buying through C&S gets invoiced by C&S at the lower net cost and C&S bills back the vendor weekly for what gets shipped to the customer. In addition to the invoice, C&S provides detailed movement information for the P-Vendor billings. These deductions are noted on the check remittance or customer invoice as P-Vendor, PVND or P&D (Pass and Deduct).
NOTE: Some indirect customer contracts may state OI, but they are billing back to C&S. As long as all other criteria match, the dollar amount, the dates, the items, it is still the correct contract. However, when the invoice AMOUNT does not match the indirect customer invoice — the C&S check remit must then be reviewed to determine if there is an additional service charge amount added for multiple invoices taken on the check remit.
The contracts used for the P-Vendor deductions would always be the indirect contract and could be found under either the C&S customer sign-on or the indirect customer sign-on. When searching for contracts, search first under the C&S customer sign-ons, then the specific indirect sign-on before escalating for contract issues. Refer to the indirect customer SOP for sign-on and customer specific information.

Scan fees.

22. Deduction Type: Off Invoice
A per case off invoice allowance is given to the customer as an automatic discount for product purchased from the client. If the customer does not receive the allowance off the face of the invoice they will deduct for it. If the customer requested an allowance that is not valid, the CSC will send a notification to the customer in writing. Customers view purchase orders as contracts. If they are not notified of allowance discrepancies, they will pay according to their purchase order total.
If an AWI indirect customer requests off invoice allowances on their customer check requests those claim lines will need to be escalated to the Client Manager (stepped as Escalate - Contract Invld Data or Contract Invld Data) so they can provide direction on how to process. CRA Client Specific
CAMPBELLS
Campbell’s/Grocers Supply is done by Inside Sales. Before stepping claims to sales for contract, etc., make sure the Client Manager is Jessica Swanson, out of Minneapolis. If it is not, change it.
CCNA
SSA deductions:
The deduction must be entered onto the SSA tracker that is available in the Microsoft TEAMS and sent to the PFA (Angela Durham – andurham@coca-cola.com)
The PFA will provide clearing instruction including event numbers and the breakdown that will be used to create the DBW
No contract
If any PO listed is not available in ACOSTA RELAY,include the PO #'s in the notes for escalation.
Below is an example of the SSA Tracker.
GEORGIA PACIFIC
Claims for Kroger division 704 may include a portion that is for C&S. This is the process that should be followed:
704 claims – the CRA will pull ATB on Mondays and look for 704 claims. If the Kroger invoice has the same UPC listed multiple times, the CRA will check to see if we have the promotional detail in AR and if so, link it to the claim. If not, the CRA will request the promotional detail from Kroger and step to 1st Request Customer Backup. (The CRA may be stepping a claim from a GCC step in this case.) The CRA will notify GP as to what portion is for Kroger and what portion is for C&S and GP will reinstate the C&S portion in TA. The CRA will then copy the claim in AR and change the customer sign-on of the 2nd claim to CSSANC.
If the store is listed as 704-798 and there are no UPCs listed more than once, the entire claim is for C&S. The CRA will change the sign-on to CSSANC, notify GP that the claim is for C&S and reinstate in TA.
Once these claims have been reinstated in TA, the claim will be processed by the CRA who handles CSSANC.
INVALID INFORMATION
C&S will be using the new portal of PayBox for all clients.  See PayBox Deduction Legend and PayBox Vendor Manual for instructions on how to submit repay letters.
The Check Coversheet Report is required to attach for all requests using the PayBox system.
For repay follow up, all deduction questions, paybox claim questions and concerns email deductionhelp@cswg.com
For status or queries on an open or past due request email openinvoice@cswg.com or call accounts payable at 802-257-6676 – the exception would be if you have already be given a PO status,or voided, invalid or zero received and you have submitted a claim or have questions on submitting a claim into PayBox.
Invalid Crossroads Incentive/SSA/Rebate claims will be sent to C&S via PayBox.  These will not be addressed to the indirect related to the buyer number or warehouse associated to the shipped order linked to the claim.
ISQL deductions submitted to Vendor Relations for review must include a copy of the Exit Pass, check cover sheet report, a BOL with a C&S signature, and Vendor Relations claim form. Including the signed BOL with your claim will allow us to provide you with an efficient response. Please note that claims submitted without proper documentation will not be processed. We thank you for your anticipated cooperation.
If a Paybox claim has been closed and needs to be reopened, add a comment to the claim. It could take up to 72 hours for the claim to be reopened. If it has not reopened after that time, email deductionhelp@cswg.com.
If the 3rd party deduction has been deemed invalid the repay letter must be sent to the indirect that was identified.  These repay letters should not be sent to C&S
Fairway Market invalid deductions that are deducted through C&S have to be mailed to Fairway not C&S.
Send to the below mailing address with attention to Liza Gonzalez – AR manager
Fairway Markets, 2284 12th Ave, New York City, NY 10027.

DOLE

Repays:

Cover letter with disputed charges
Copy of all PO invoices (if multiple invoices on a PO)
Copy of Debit memo/receipt information provided
Copy of all CVS signed proof of deliveries to show complete PO invoices & goods were signed/shipped in full.
If disputing pricing, please forward pricing agreement/notification of CVS of change.
Post Audit Repays are sent to: PRAudit@CVSHealth.com
CVS Portal Access: Click the link below.
CVS Health - Vendor Portal
Only non-trade is disputed by PRS in portal.  Trade related disputes are sent to Acosta sales for submission

sections.content:
Customer Invoice Info:

MDI deducts on behalf 8 indirect customers. Refer to the Indirect Info section.
Merchant customer invoice prefixes:
D Damage/Unsaleable
GR Merchants customer invoice(other prefixes can be present see indirect info section).
Can include indirect related customer invoice information. See Indirect Info section.
If deducting on behalf of the indirect there will be two invoice numbers. The first one will start with GR and the secondary will not begin with GR.
The indirect customer name can also be listed on the body of the invoice. If both invoice numbers are the same then the claim is for MDI direct.
FEES:
Indirect customer fees, claims for indirect customer may not match the claim header because it does not include the $50.00 (indirect invoices $60 and over) or $100.00 (below $60) Admin Fee. This fee is added later by MDI when billing the vendor. If the Invoice total does not match the claim header total, and is off by $50.00/$100.00 Admin Fee, it is ok to validate the $50.00/$100.00 Admin Fee as an admin fee.
PALLETS- Inbound product should be shipped on 40x48 four-way entry oak GMA Grade B or better, CHEP, or PECO pallets in good condition

MDI Pass-Thru (Pre-Paid):
Claims created from a customer invoice are pre-paid (pass-thru) claims. This is a bucket of money set aside by the client to have money pulled from vs. the customer deducting from a check. Client event numbers are not required for these claims, even if the client requires an event number, one is not required for a pre-paid claim. Event scheduler contracts may have “PASS THRU – NO EVENT” loaded as the event.
The only time a client event number will be required is if the pre-paid fund is depleted and MDI has to deduct. If the fund is depleted then claims will create from the ATB or a client deduction notice. There will be a $$50.00/$100.00 Admin Fee deduction fee.
Due to pass thru customer invoices creating claims, it is possible a duplicate warning will prompt if the customer deducts due to depleted funds. The ATB/CDN claim needs to be stepped to escalate repay issue and noted accordingly. The CRA needs to check the pass thru statements to make sure this invoice wasn’t taken from the pass thru account. If the customer invoice did not come from the pass thru, the CRA will request that the ATB/CDN claim is stepped to the GCC to validate the claim.

A per case off invoice allowance (OI) is given to the customer as an automatic discount for product purchased from the client. If they are not notified of allowance discrepancies, they will pay according to their purchase order total.

Purchase Order Vendor invoice reconciliation
To ensure invoices are paid accurately, Publix reconciles the prices and quantity for each Product on the invoice against the cost offers previously submitted by the Supplier and the quantities entered into our receiving systems at the time of delivery. It is imperative every component of the cost structure on the Vendor invoice match the cost offer submitted by the Supplier exactly. Failure to submit costs as they will be invoiced will result in inaccurate payments to the Supplier.
Publix processes invoices for payment based on the product received during the check in process supported by valid proof of delivery.
Discrepancies between the direct store delivery (DSD) Supplier invoice and the Publix generated invoice can result from cost or pack differences, shortages, damages, or the attempted delivery of unauthorized Products. The driver is responsible for making the necessary corrections to the Supplier’s invoice and forwarding this information to the appropriate department within the Supplier’s organization.
Temporary shelf price reductions
Temporary shelf price reductions (TPRs) are Publix promotions where the retail price of a Product is reduced for a specified period of time (usually two to eight weeks). These price reductions may be communicated to our customers using a special shelf tag. Suppliers requesting a TPR promotion must provide a temporary cost reduction for the Product being promoted that is sufficient to warrant a retail reduction.
Accounting portal
Suppliers are required to enroll in the Publix Taulia Accounting portal after they are set up as a new supplier in the Publix systems. Features and benefits of this system include:• Free to enroll and view your invoices and payment info• 24/7 visibility to your account• Invoice status• Ability to list/search for purchase orders, invoices, and credits• Communicate with Publix through the portal messaging boardOnce enrolled, you may expand access to others within your organization. For additional information and to enroll in the portal, please view our Publix Taulia Welcome website at http://supplier.taulia.com/customers/publix/

1         Deduction Type: Off Invoice
A per case off invoice allowance is given to the customer as an automatic discount for product purchased from the client. If the customer does not receive the allowance off the face of the invoice they will deduct for it. If the customer requested an allowance that is not valid, the CSC will send a notification to the customer in writing. Customers view purchase orders as contracts. If they are not notified of allowance discrepancies, they will pay according to their purchase order total.
Customer Invoice for Off Invoice, Example 1: Non EDI format (This Check Remittance serves as their Customer Invoice):
UPC Code – The universal product code (UPC) is 5 digits from the last number. This code is used to validate key data elements regarding the customer invoice and client order invoice on the Review Order/view document link within ACOSTA Relay. This is the product in which the customer is stating that there is an off invoice allowance.Eg: In this case the UPC is the one highlighted in red 1002389617700.UPC Code – The universal product code (UPC) is 5 digits from the last number. This code is used to validate key data elements regarding the customer invoice and client order invoice on the Review Order/view document link within ACOSTA Relay. This is the product in which the customer is stating that there is an off invoice allowance.Eg: In this case the UPC is the one highlighted in red 1002389617700.Adj Diff – The amount listed is the amount which the customer has deducted as part of the off invoice. In this case the deduction amount is $655.00.Divide the Adj diff amount by ADJ QTY to arrive at rate per case OI allowance.Adj Diff – The amount listed is the amount which the customer has deducted as part of the off invoice. 10.Deduction Type:  Ad
A fee for featuring a client's products in an advertisement.
Weekly ads:
Publix may publish a weekly ad and distribute versions of this ad in various markets. Weekly ads represent a significant promotion vehicle available at Publix because they generally generate increased sales volume. Publix expects our stores to display all featured and buy-one get-one (BOGO) Products in Publix’s weekly ads. Suppliers shall ensure that Publix is provided with sufficient quantities of all products included in the weekly ad to prevent out-of-stock situations.
Suppliers are expected to provide promotional funding for retail price reductions for Products included in the weekly ad. This funding shall include the Supplier reimbursing Publix for the promotional allowance or discount for any rainchecks provided by Publix up to thirty (30) days after the expiration of the weekly ad. Publix shall have the right to deduct such amounts from future payments to the Supplier.
NOTE:  If the customer deducts for an ad and the ad date listed on the customer invoice will not run within the timeline duration of Long Term POP (45 calendar days), the CRA will need to use the step of Pending Performance and set an Outlook reminder to address the claim when the ad is to run per the dates on the customer’s invoice.

Post Audits
Payments audit policy
In our continuing effort to provide our customers superior value, Publix performs post payment audits of all payments and billings made to our Suppliers. We perform this audit in accordance with the guidelines set
forth below and we expect all Suppliers to comply with these guidelines.
Post payment audit policy
Publix complies with the Food Marketing Institute (FMI)/Grocery Manufacturers Association (GMA) Invoice Deduction Guidelines concerning post payment audit claims for pricing and promotional discrepancies. Therefore, our goal is to submit all post payment audit claims within 24 months from the end of the calendar year of the deal.
However, Publix reserves the right, as protected under applicable statutes of limitations, to submit post payment audit claims within 48 months of the deal.
Making post payment audit claims
When a discrepancy is found, Publix Payments Audit department will follow the guidelines below to process the claim and recover the funds.
• Publix deducts post payment audit claims from current payments to the Supplier. However, Publix reserves the right to bill the Supplier for balances that cannot be deducted from current payments.
• With each post payment audit claim submitted, Publix includes appropriate back-up documentation to support the claim. Publix will not provide documentation that was previously sent to Publix by the Supplier (i.e., original invoices) or previously sent by Publix to the Supplier (i.e., check remittances).
Disputing post payment audit claims
Suppliers must comply with the following guidelines when disputing a post payment audit claim.
• Publix submits post payment audit claims to our Suppliers in writing via hard copy or electronic media. Suppliers must communicate all disputes to Publix in the same manner.
• Publix responds to all disputes within 30 days. If we receive no additional communication from the Supplier within 60 days of our response, we consider the dispute resolved.
Promotion funds
Suppliers cannot deduct post payment audit claims from current year promotional funds.

Customer Invoice Info
Is line level detail indexed on the customer’s documentation (Customer Invoice, Customer Check Request, Unsaleable/Spoils, Post Audit, EDI 812/820 or Client Deduction Notice if one of these documents is included)?  YES
It is imperative that the repository and portals are searched thoroughly under all necessary signons and divisions due to Savemart charging $50 for each duplicate copy of backup that is sent.
Note:  SaveMart/Food Maxx does not always supply any support documentation (Customer Invoice explaining why they are deducting) for PO Related claims:  including Off Invoice, Billback, Pricing and Cash Discount.  You must pull the Client Order Invoice and back into the claim.
You will need to review and follow the directions provided in the job aids listed below. These are located on Acosta Relay main screen under Claims then SOP Documents.
PO Related Claims
Pricing Deduction Job Aid
Cash Discount Job Aid
**Please review the order found under View Documents of the Review Order Screen to determine which customer the order shipped to.
If, for these invoices, you are able to validate the majority as a BB or OI, GCC should split off the part that cannot be validated and escalate for Customer Invoice.  Likewise, if no part of the PO can be validated, GCC should escalate for Customer Invoice.
Food Maxx will use their original purchase order (PO) to reference bill backs.  This may be used to identify the QTY and allowances the customer is deducting for and assist in locating the contract.  Locate the PO in ACOSTA RELAY using the Orders/Invoices/PO search screen.  Under View Documents, at the top of the PO screen, a copy of the original order may be located under the Active Documents section.  The contract will be the same as the purchase order, but must be indexed as a contract in ACOSTA RELAY for use in validation.
Cross Dock items are products that Food Maxx ordered which is crossing the Save Mart dock and being loaded on a truck going to Food Maxx.  The product being ordered/cross docked is NOT a stock item in the Save Mart warehouse.  The contract will be a Food Maxx contract.
Invoices may be indexed under any of the customer sign ons.  These should be searched for by replacing the prefix (DEAL, RDS) with the wildcard (%) on the Backup Documentation search screen.
Spoils/Unsaleables may begin with the prefix PRC or SUN.   However, not all PRC invoices are for spoils.  Those ending in DM or A are debit memos and copies must be requested via the backup procedures outlined in the BPS Team information section.
Save Mart will take deductions for allowances offered on products that were cut from orders.  These deductions are called “shorted deals”.  These allowances may be Off Invoice or Bill Back, or other types of allowances.  There should be a contract for these products and allowances.  SEE EXAMPLE NEXT PAGE
Save Mart will only use each DEAL # once.  The “P” at the end of DEALxxxxxP stands for Partial Payment due to not enough funds.  These will result in a split deduction (more than one claim tied to the customer invoice).  The Customer Invoice will not have the P included on the invoice number.
Invoice numbers ending in F are for the fee C&S charges when deducting on behalf of an indirect. The check remittance will indicate "service fee".  There will be no separate invoice for reference numbers ending in 'F' and these claims should not be escalated for missing invoice.  See below for more information in Other General Info.
Contract Info:
Save Mart is an Acoustic DemandTec customer.  an Acoustic DemandTec Contracts/Deal Sheets have a reference number that may be used to identify which store the deduction belongs to and assist in locating the contract. These numbers are listed on the customer invoice as the Deal #.  The first 3 numbers indicate the division:
710 = Save Mart
810 = Food Maxx
910 = Lucky’s
NOTE:  Some contracts are generated outside of Acoustic DemandTec. These may be located under any of the sign ons listed in the box above.
When searching for the Acoustic DemandTec contract use the Deal Sheet # listed on the invoice minus the letters at the end.  These letters (SSI,VAC,STK etc) should not be included when completing the search in AR or entered in the Check # field when requesing contracts to be downloaded.
Even though the last letters will not be used when searching or requesting contracts to be downloaded, these letters should match on the invoice and the contract. If the VPF and the contract is not available in AR for the correct division (SSI, VAC, etc) step to sales for the contract.  Effective 9/15/24 Save Mart, Lucky, and Food Maxx are owned by C&S the contract will include the STK abbreviation.
Speed Fee contracts will not have the $6.00 fee listed on their contracts.
POP Info:
For Sales Analysis Reporting  - Since SaveMart/Yosemite or FoodMaxx can purchase product direct from the client or pull product from a direct customer, the report needs to be ran using all of the following customer signons:  FOOMNC, SAVENC and SPRSNC.  Note – Save Mart also owns FoodMaxx & Lucky’s.
Refer to the Proof of Performance Reporting Ads job aid for searching for ads.
Other General Info:
Refer to the C&S SOP for fee examples.

Military invoices reference MDV or have a reference number beginning with ST.  The invoice may also have the following letters following it that would also indicate it is for Military: SA (Salvage), DE (Destroy, NEX (Nexcom), RA (Return), EP (European Pallet), FS (Fuel Surcharge).
Amazon claims are Not Acosta.
NMC on an invoice = MW Corporate Retail.
Customer invoices that reference ‘FFS’ or ‘FFARE’ are billing for Family Fares in the West (Omaha).
When claims come in with a customer reference number beginning 2915, it is an indication of a NFLBRA claim.
If claim is indexed to something other than NFLBRA, it should be changed.  Look in backup documentation for another invoice with the customer reference numbers without the 2915 prefix on the invoice in the customer reference number field.
For example, the claim has 29159643 and this invoice has 9643 (everything but the 2915). Also, the invoice may be indexed under the indirect name on this invoice, if it is not under NFLBRA.
This is the invoice with the detail for the claim.  It will have 2 pages, at least.  This deduction will always have a $25 fee from Nash Finch.
Refer to client SOP for instructions on breaking out the fee.
The CRA should contact the CBM on the line for the complete invoice, if it is not in ACOSTA Relay.
If the customer invoice contains an Acoustic DemandTec number, use the alpha characters to identify which region’s contract to use and search for a contract using the numeric portion.
SpartanNash offers PVA (Preferred Vendor Agreements) and any client identified as PVA will only receive Count Recount/Warehouse Withdrawal offers.  They will not be offered/receive direct shipment billbacks.
EFT/Check Remit
For PO related claims, the EFT (electronic funds transfers) and/or check remittance may also provide details.  It can be used as an invoice if the document gives the UPCs needed to search for the contract.  With the contract, you will be able to determine the details of the claim.  Review the document before requesting backup.
If the EFT/check remittance has no information to help you determine the details of the claim, the cliam must have an invoice to validate.
If the EFT/check remittance references the deductions as freight, a customer invoice will be needed.
If the EFT/check remit has a Bus Unit Code column and ‘NFC’ or ‘SFS’ is in that field, the claim is for Nash Finch.
A check remit number is required on the Nash Finch backup request form, entered under the Payment # field on the form.  The check remit number from the Check Remittance # field in the claim header is often incorrect.  The check remit must be used to confirm the correct check remit #.  Do not use the number from the check remit field without first confirming it is correct.
When filling out the backup request form, the Invoice Number must be entered as it shows on the check remit.  Note that some clients send over a portion of the customer invoice number.
The vendor number is not required, but should be used if available on the check remittance.
Scan invoices that includes the contract number and the same contract number followed by an “A”. The “A” represents the 2nd week of billing and there will not be an additional contract found for the “A”.
DBW Info:
Nash Finch will sometimes add small amounts to their invoices that are for freight and have nothing to do with a promotion. See below:
These small amounts should be added up and put on a separate line in the claim.  Use FREIGHT as the entry info for the DBW.  This may be used to capture all these small amounts as one line item.
Contract Info:
SpartanNash is an Acoustic DemandTec customer.
When alerting for a missing Acoustic VPF/Contract, add the alpha code SN in front of the numeric portion of the Acoustic# in the check # field.
Searching for contracts:
If contracts are not found under the master sign-on, use the division sign-on.
Sioux Falls and Bellefontaine may have VPFs because they ship orders, but no contracts are created for them.
Sioux Falls will use any contract from the Midwest.
Bellefontaine uses any Great Lakes contract.
Occasionally, Nash Finch sends an invoice with no promotion dates – only an invoice date.  These could be billback or count/recount invoices.  For count/recount invoices, you will need to search for contracts with dates directly before the date on the invoice, or that include the date of the invoice.  For BB invoices, search for the Client Order Invoice.  This will have order and ship dates, which will assist in the contract search.
Indirect customers of Nash Finch may have different billing dates than the contract. (Contracts are created for the entire region of NF.)  As long as these dates vary by no more than 5 days, this is acceptable.
Lump sum fees are always on the Spartan contract unless Spartan doesn’t carry the item; then it will be under Nash Finch.
Ad Fees on contracts are not nescessarily for Ads, the dollar amount determines what the lumpsum is for.
$10,000 = PB
$3,000 = WAV/BOV
$3,000 = TPR
$5,000 = Buy Big Save Big
$2,000 = EDLP
$7,000 = E-Ad
Fargo Division and indirect customer Hugo’s contracts – Some clients, but not all, are on a special “Low/EDLP Program” for Fargo/Hugo’s, meaning that all of the contracts for the Fargo division are created separately in Acoustic DemandTec from the other division contracts for the clients that are on this special program. If the Fargo division contract is not among the other division contracts, a separate search will need to be completed for the stand alone Fargo division contract (NASFMN); which will be under a different Relay event #. You may have to do multiple searches and might have multiple contracts for a singe claim.
POP Info:
Sales Analysis Reports are run using the sign-ons for the entire region as listed on the Nash Finch sign-on job aid.
When a customer invoice lists GMS, IRI data can be pulled for any or all regions and divisions.  GMS supports all of Nash Finch.
Ads are found in FeatureVision using Family Fare, D&W and VG’s, Glen’s or may be attached to the CCR.  If the claim is for a check request and an ad is required but not included with the check request packet, the ad is requested from the customer manager.  Use Harding’s for non-corporate ads (ad fee is $6000 for non-corporate).
When a contract states ‘Yes’ for ‘Is Offer on Ad?’ and the comments state the ad fee is listed on a different contract, an ad is not required for the unit/case rate allowance.
Chiefs and Fresh Encounters are a part of Spartan. Their ads can be used for validation.
Other General Info:
SpartanNash has indirects that will submit check requests.  Unpaid check requests are not automatically deducted, but can be if the sales team advises them to.
Postage is a non-trade administrative fee.  Please refer to the client SOP as how to deal with this.
Below is the 2018 Fiscal Year Calendar and Indirect Sign-ons and Ad dates.
SpartanNash has a 90-day Center Store cost increase notice and 60-day notice for Fresh, see attached Cost policy, Cost Management Vendor Procedures, and Cost Change Request Form.
Please see attached information regarding SpartanNash’s Locations and DUNS, Military DUNS and SpartanNash DC by Channel.
ReposiTrak system: SpartanNash has moved to a volume-based fee structure for the Repositrak service. Annual fees are now determined by the annual sales volume of each vendor’s business with SpartanNash. See attached letters explaining what Repositrack is and for pricing tiers.
No additional support will be provided for Repositrak claims.
Reclamation and Recall Handling Fee Policies – Effective July 5, 2026

A per case billback allowance is claimed by the direct buying customer for product purchased from the client, or by the indirect customer for product purchased from the direct customer.  This is an allowance the customer will bill the client for.  This is not an automatic discount given off the face of the invoice.

7.Deduction Type: Slotting
A Slotting allowance is offered to the customer to purchase an item not currently stocked. It is a kind of promotional money offered to a customer as incentive to buy a new item and create a “slot” for that product on their warehouse storage shelves. It is a Trade Deduction. A slotting lump sum allowance can be offered for each item and/or an off invoice can be offered as an introductory allowance for the first 30 days.
Nash Finch receives a lump sum for slotting for each region. This amount is broken up by Nash Finch to distribute to each DC. It does not matter how much is given to each DC, as long as the total lump sum allowed is not surpassed. If Nash Finch takes slotting money from one region and applies it to a different region, this must be approved by the Business Manager.

title: UNFI Conventional SOP
description: Claims processing and backup retrieval procedures for UNFI Conventional (conventional grocery) accounts.

sections.title: DEDUCTION TYPES COVERED
sections.content:
Is the customer a wholesaler/distributor, direct or indirect customer? Direct Wholesaler
UNFI Conventional (UNFI Conventional (SuperValu)) sign-ons used for claims entry and backup documentation indexing are below:
ZZNASVMN – Master sign-on
SUPMMN – Central Region
SUPHRM – Eastern Region
SUPVBI – South Region (formerly SE) or SERF
SVFLMI – Florida Region (formerly known as Associated Grocers Miami – ASSOMI), and Krasdale / Beta II / Bravo indirects
SVTACBL – Tacoma
SUPEPT – Portland
SUPCBL – Centralia
SVCSDB – SoCal/Commerce
SVSTNC – NoCal/ Stockton
UWGRLI – Market Centre Norcal
UWGRPN – Market Centre Pacific NorthWest (PNW) include Seattle
UWGRSC – Market Centre SoCal
Change the customer sign-on to the correct region’s/indirect sign-on see the UNFI Conventional (SuperValu) Signon Job Aid. The set of location numbers on the customer reference number will determine which customer sign-on to use.
UNFI Conventional sign-ons for contracts and POP are listed in the UNFI Conventional Signon Job Aid:
LINK TO CUSTOMER SIGN-ON JOB AID:
https://acostaonline.sharepoint.com/sites/AS_Reporting/Claims_Reports/Forms/AllItems.aspx?web=1
Does this customer subscribe to IRI/Nielsen for price point verification? Yes for the following customers:
SV Eastern
SV Central
SV Seattle/NR/Tacoma (Unified Seattle)
SV Socal (Unified Socal).
However, UNFI Conventional is a distributor and does not normally deduct on its own behalf. All deductions from UNFI Conventional (except some slotting and WAREHOUSE BILLBACK) are taken on behalf of an indirect. These indirects do not subscribe to IRI/Nielsen and price point verification will not be available.

UNFI charges a higher RFT Fee (lump sum) for the primary ad item and charges a discounted RFT Fee for the bundled ad item(s). sections.title: PROCESS STEPS
sections.content:
1.Deduction Type: Off Invoice
A per-case off invoice allowance is given to the customer as an automatic discount for product purchased from the client. If the customer does not receive the allowance off the face of the invoice they will deduct for it. The below fees will be standard these fees may vary by client.
Item set-up fees
$2500 per DC standard rate for all new items including conversions and pack changes.
In and out items (pallets, shippers and seasonal limited time items) are $500 per DC.

21.Deduction Type: Deducted Check Request/Indirect Deduction
There are indirect customers who purchase product through wholesalers (i.e. UNFI Conventional) that are offered promotional allowances on contracts. Most of these indirect customers require a check for payment since they cannot deduct from the client because they do not order directly from them. If the indirect customer does not receive payment within a specified time period (reflected on the customer’s invoice), they may deduct through the wholesaler. The UNFI Conventional (SuperValu) invoice will detail the indirect customer and the invoice number(s) for which they are deducting. There are some indirect customers for which UNFI Conventional automatically deducts.
IF THE UNFI CONVENTIONAL (SUPERVALU) INVOICE REFERENCES AN INDIRECT AND THE INDIRECT’S INVOICE NUMBER, THE INDIRECT INVOICE MUST BE LINKED TO THE CLAIM. Please note that there may be more than one invoice number being deducted.

The dates on the contract may not match completely the dates of the period on the fiscal calendar, but this mismatch is acceptable because the customer is identifying the period where there are contracts that have a missed allowance.
