sections.title: CUSTOMER GENERAL INFORMATION
sections.content:
Customer Invoice Info:
Is line level detail indexed on the customer’s documentation (customer invoice, customer check request, unsaleable/spoils, post audit, EDI 812/820) or client deduction notice if one of these documents is included? Yes.
UNFI acquired Hadden House warehouses all claims will be worked in AR under UNINNN including contract and POP searches.
MCB claims can have multiple allowance types listed on the UNFI customer invoice in multiple combinations.  Each type of allowance may require a separate contract.
West Coast UNFI Invoice codes:
A – Authorized by Vendor (EDLP – see Warehouse Withdrawal/Count Recount section)
C – Show Deals  (see Warehouse Withdrawal/Count Recount section)
E – EDLP (see Warehouse Withdrawal/Count Recount section)
F – UNFI NC and HA Circulars (see Ad section)
M – New Additions (see Slotting section)
O – New Store Opening/Placement (see Slotting section)
P – UNFI Monthly Special (see Warehouse Withdrawal/Count Recount section)
S – Shelf Sales (see Warehouse Withdrawal/Count Recount section)
T – Turnover (see Slotting section if allowance is over 35%, see Warehouse Withdrawal/Count Recount section if allowance is 35% and under)
U – UNFI Events
X – Samples
Z – Miscellaneous  (deduction type will be based on contract)
East  Coast UNFI Invoice codes:
A – Arranged by Vendor (see Warehouse Withdrawal/Count Recount section)
C – Case Stack (see Warehouse Withdrawal/Count Recount section)
D – Demo (see Warehouse Withdrawal/Count Recount section)
M – Miscellaneous  (deduction type will be based on contract)
N – Mass Mkt Opening/Placement (see Slotting section)
O – Opening Order  (see Slotting section)
P – Promos  (see Warehouse Withdrawal/Count Recount section)
S – Show Order (see Warehouse Withdrawal/Count Recount section)
T – Turnover Order (see Slotting section if allowance is over 35%, see Warehouse Withdrawal/Count Recount section if allowance is 35% and under)
U – UNFI Events
Z – Samples
The customer invoice will be used to determine if deduction is West or East.  However if the location cannot be determined by the customer invoice the Check Remit can be linked to help determine location:
if the Check Remit address (upper left hand corner) states Keene, NH, (considered UNFI East)  the Customer Sign On will need to be changed to UNINNN.
Invoices may include some clues if it is a East or West deduction or deduction type:
Claims with the prefix of WE is a UNFI EAST MCB
Claims with the prefix MCB is a UNFI West MCB
Claims with the prefix CMQ is an unsaleable
Claims with the prefix WR is a west region
Claims with the prefix ER is an East region
If the customer reference number contains the word “Raleys”, the customer sign on needs to be updated to one of the following depending on the client:
RALENC (for Grocery Clients)
RALELI (for Natural Specialty Clients)
If invoice states Price Chopper and does not specify Golub, process as AWG.
Please refer to the attached spreadsheet for additional information regarding invoice information:  Please note the prefixes noted on the below spreadsheet is in reference to the customer reference # not the chain acronyms on an MCB invoice.
Pre-Pay deductions
Pre-Pay claims (Invoice ex. 0001085895PP):
Pre-Pays are not deductions and will NOT have any backup documentation except for Check Remit and Client Order Invoice.
UNFI is pre-paying the client prior to receiving the PO in order to receive the cash discount. The amount will usually be 1% of the total client order invoice amount. If claim amount is not reflecting cash discount amount or 1% of total invoice amount, email deductions@unfi.com and erap@unfi.com to find out why it was short paid.
Pre-Pay details:
· PO related
· Only backup documentation available are the Check Remit, Order Invoice, and the Customer PO.
· After prepayment goes out, UNFI then compares the invoice to what was actually received and make a final payment with the corrected dollar amount after researching the shipment.
· If the prepayment is on any other date, the payment is based on the face value of the invoice then adjusted accordingly to the research UNFI conducts on the PO.
DBW Info:
When creating a DBW for UNFI claims if multiple indirect customers are deducting through UNFI the DBW should be updated with the name of the customer or appropriate abbreviation in the promo event field.
Only the abbreviations listed in the Indirect Customer Chain Acronyms under the Customer Invoice information may be used when creating the DBWs. Please do not use the ones listed in parenthesis on the Customer Invoice as these customers may not be on the same Contracts. See examples below:
The store names in these examples should be:  St. Peter Food Coop, Good Foods Coop, Lexington Coop, Company Shops Market, respectively.The store names in these examples should be:  St. Peter Food Coop, Good Foods Coop, Lexington Coop, Company Shops Market, respectively.
If the customer provides an Excel invoice or if using the MCB macro to create the DBW UPCs can be combined into one line, if the rates, indirect customer,performance dates, and claim type match for all UPCs that are being grouped together.
If there are no client specific directions on how to sort the DBW in either the client specific section or the client SOP use the sort by claim line option.
Contract Info:
If a UNFI national deal is offered to the East and the West, the West deals should match with the East, however, you should be able to find a Contract for both regions.  A National contract can be used to clear all regions, not just East and West.
Contracts will offer a % or $ amount allowance on the contract.  To confirm the correct contract calculate take the Cost on CI multiply by the % allowance on the contract, this will give you the rate.  If the allowance is calculated based off the unit cost (Unit Cost $1.647 x 12 Units) x 15% = $2.96 BUT  On the contract it shows $.25/Unit  x 12 units = $3.00/cs.  This contract can still be considered as valid.
If the calculation is not equal to or less than the contract allowance and the invoice has an allowance in a decimal format ($.36) or percentage formant (15%) then the contract needs to match the allowance format on the CI.
When locating a contract for an indirect customer please refer to the Indirect Customer listing includes information for additional contract signons.
Deals such as MCBs (Manufacturer Chargebacks), scans, etc. are offered by Region and by Distribution Center.
Note – If the customer has a formal SOP please see Formal SOP for additional information on locating contract and viewing contract examples.
Refer to the Indirect customer job aid for the listing of customers  or the letters CGA, CMW, CNE, or NCG after the customer name on the invoice indicates that the customer is a member of the National Cooperative Grocers Association.  This is a Co-op, containing many stores in all regions East and West.  The Contract needed to validate this portion of the deduction will be a NCGA contract located under the ZZCAPNNN.
Refer to the Indirect customer job aid for the listing of customers  or the letters INF after the customer name on the invoice indicates that this customer is a member of the INFRA group which contains customers in all regions (East and West).  The contract needed to validate this portion of the deduction will be an INFRA contract.
Refer to the Indirect customer job aid for the listing of customers that are part of the ION group coop.  The contract needed to validate this portion of the deduction will be an ION (Its Only Natural) contract.
UNFI purchased Trudeau Foods (Minnesota, Wisconsin, North Dakota).  Some contracts may still say Trudeau, but are valid to clear UNFI deductions for customers in these regions (Lunds, Byerly’s, etc) if the products, dates, rates match.
New Leaf and New Seasons are part of the same company – Contracts for either company can either be located under NEWSPN or ZZNEWLLI.
Contracts and invoices may not include dates but will include a cycle time / period.  When comparing for dates ensure the same cycle / period is mentioned on both documents.  The UNFI Conventional, UNFI calendars can be used to identify the dates for periods.
Invoice
Detailed Indirect Invoice
Invoice may not spell out Cycle but will mention a C # or just the cycle number in the description.Invoice may not spell out Cycle but will mention a C # or just the cycle number in the description.
Contract
Before escalating a claim please ensrue that the line notes include the indirect customer.
Other General Info:
United Natural Foods Inc Policies and Procedures:
United Natural Foods charges an Administration Fee for Reclaimation Invoices.  These fees are listed on a separate invoice ending in DPC.  No backup is provided, just the invoice number on the check remit.  The policy is to charge 20% of the cost of the reclaimed products, subject to a maximum fee charge per banner per month of $250, and a minimum charge per banner of $10 per month.
UNFI will assess a 3% service level fee to supplies that do not meet the 95% fill rate of all purchase orders.  They will apply the 3% only to the shored product based on the 95% fill rate. (Please see document above service level assesement fee for more information).

sections.title: BACKUP RETRIEVAL INFORMATION
sections.content:
GENERAL BACKUP RETRIEVAL INFORMATION

If yes, is there a customer portal?  No

If yes, is the check remittance number required? Yes

All other backup should be requested from the client. Email jblanco@kikkoman.com
Mezzetta
If backup documentation for UNFI claims is not available in AR, GCIT should escalate the claim onshore so that CRA can request it from the client.
Michael Angelos, Noosa, Raos
Post audits deductions that require additional detailed backup, if post audit document includes a specific contact, include a line note with the contact information and step the claim to GCIT.
Nature Delivered INC. (Graze)
Customer backup is requested from Natalie Hamilton at Nhamilton@acosta.com
Preferred Brands

If the customer does not receive the allowance off the face of the invoice they will deduct for it. REPAY / CRA INFORMATION SECTION
REPAYS
Invalid deductions:
A form is required for all disputes to UNFI.  The form must be filled out completely and emailed. The form needs to stay in the original format when sent to UNFI in order to be accepted by the UNFI system.  This form may have to be submitted separately from the repay packet.
The form includes three tabs.
Tab 1 provides instructions for how to use the form, definitions for required fields, and overall best practices.
Tab 2 is the new dispute form. Required cells offer instructions upon hovering over the cell and will be kicked back if not filled in.
Tab 3 is an additional sheet to be used as needed.
The following information must be included in the email subject line:
The word “Dispute”
Brand name
Check #
Deduction Invoice #
Dispute amount
All corresponding documents should also be attached to the email.
Repays should be sent to the following email address:  SupplierDeductionDisputeMgmt@unfi.com. This is for both East and West divisions.
UNFI will issue a tracking number for the dispute – note this tracking number on the claim.
Example of email sent from UNFI.
Unfi will send a Weekly Status Update Report each Tuesday evening, that will track the status of all disputes.
To receive a copy of this weekly report.  Email SupplierDeductionDisputeMgmt@unfi.com with your Remit # and the email(s) that need to receive this report.  Include Status Report Email Addition in the subject line,.
To follow up on the request send a request to SupplierDeductionDisputeMgmt@unfi.com include the tracking number.
If the client is a ClearVue supplier (see the client specific validation section for details if client is not a ClearVue supplier).

sections.content:
Customer Invoice Info:
Is line level detail indexed on the customers documentation (customer invoice, customer check request, unsalable/spoils, post audit, EDI 812/820 or client deduction notice if one of these documents is included)? No.
Customer Invoice Number will start with a “K” followed by numbers.  When the deduction comes through the customer reference number on the claim will begin with a “D” followed by the same numbers (see example below).  If the numbers and the amount on the invoice matches the claim amount this is the correct invoice.  Invoices are generally indexed by the  customer reference number starting with D.
URM may deduct on behalf of Rosauers and when this occurs a 2% handling fee is added to the invoice total.  Rosauers invoices/customer reference number will begin with an “R”.
DBW Info:
Total Proposal Dollars for the proposal could be offered as an AD lump sum or TPR lump sum.  These lump sums should be broken out on the Claims Processing Screen and the DBW as a separate claim detail line.  Do not include in the Admin Fee Section in the upper left corner, must be entered as a line item with the corresponding promotion number.
Please note - each section on the invoice can potentially be a separate proposal/contract number, a different indirect customer, and different types of allowances.  Each proposal/contract would be split into a separate claim detail line.  Be sure to use the contract to confirm the type of allowance.

Deduction Type: Off Invoice
A per case off invoice allowance is given to the customer as an automatic discount for product purchased from the client. If the customer does not receive the allowance off the face of the invoice they will deduct for it. If the customer requested an allowance that is not valid, the CSC will send a notification to the customer in writing. Customers view purchase orders as contracts. If they are not notified of allowance discrepancies, they will pay according to their purchase order total.

2.Deduction Type: Bill Back
A Bill Back claim is a per case allowance offered for a specific performance requirement. A per case billback allowance is claimed by the direct buying customer for product purchased from the client, or by the indirect customer for product purchased from the direct customer. This is an allowance the customer will bill the client for. This is not an automatic discount given off the face of the invoice.
If contract is listing an Indirect Customer (example:  Rosauers, Harvest Foods, Yokes, etc or an Ad Group) a Sales Summary is sufficient.
However, if contract is for URM Stores Inc, a Memo Tracker is needed and not a Sales Summary.

sections.title: CUSTOMER GENERAL INFORMATION
sections.content:
Customer Invoice Info:
Is line level detail indexed on the customer’s documentation (customer invoice, customer check request, unsaleable/spoils, post audit, EDI 812/820 or client deduction notice if one of these documents is included)? Yes
Wakefern invoices can only be pulled from the Wakefern proprietary system.
High Radius pulls backup from the customer’s proprietary system and searches daily by date to obtain the check remit and customer invoice details from the Wakefern portal, including a copy of the customer invoice. The backup is uploaded into the repository daily.
On certain customer invoices obtained from the Wakefern portal, the customer reference # in AR may not be listed on the customer invoice.  In this case, the number is obtained from the check remit information in the customer portal.
Claims may be created in ACOSTA Relay with either the PO # or the Client Order Invoice number listed in the Customer Reference # field, depending how the information is sent in by the client. When searching for the backup, if unable to locate the documentation in AR using the customer reference number, search using the customer reference number in the client reference number field.
Some invoices may be indexed with line level details that are not displayed on the invoice but were obtained from the customer portal.
Price Plus detailed backup is being pulled by High Radius.  The backup will be attached to the invoice as an embedded Excel file, so the paperclip will be used to view the document.  If the Excel file is not present for Price Plus invoices, the claim needs to be stepped to GCIT to pull the detailed backup.
Wakefern uses various terms to refer to one kind of claim.  Lock Net, Locked Cost, Ad Lock. And Price Lock are all the same thing; the terminology varies by department.  Wakefern will not supply item detail to support Lock Net invoices.  If item detail is required, it can be obtained via a sales report from ACOSTA Relay or a shipment report from the client’s system.  Detail cannot be requested from Wakefern. For Grocery Wholesale  invoices, invoices for Wakefern’s indirect wholesalers, no contracts are needed. These invoices can be cleared with just an event number.
Price Rite Invoices
Price Rite does not provide detailed invoices.
If there is a discrepancy between the total amount billed for Price Plus invoice and the total of the backup included on the detail pages, the missing portion could be for Price Rite, for which there is no detailed backup. Best practice would be for the GCC to escalate only the portion of the difference of the customer invoice dollar amount so the CRA can research. If the invoice does not reference Price Rite, then the CRA will need to confirm with sales the missing portion of the invoice is caused by Price Rite.
If any of the following scenarios applies for the Price Rite invoices, then sales will need to provide a percentage breakdown by either category or UPC (depending on how the client clears) to continue with validation.  Note: If this percentage can be applied to the category/UPC for every invoice, then log an SOP ticket to have it added to the Client Specific section.
If the products listed on the contract have multiple rates
or
If the products listed on the contract have multiple categories
or
If the client requires math by the UPC level or clears at the UPC level.
Price Rite Alt Cost MM/DD/YY or Specialty Alt Cost MM/DD/YY invoices:
Do not require contracts.
No additional back up is available.
Claim is coded as Scan.
Contract Info:
Price Rite
Price Rite is an indirect of Wakerfern.  There are no Price Rite contracts.
Price Rite does not have any scan capabilities, so they take the agreed upon Price Plus or scan and convert it into a billback.  Price Rite gets 50% of the Price Plus value and handling in a case rate.  To calculate the allowance, take the Price Plus contract rate, multiply by the number of units in the case and then multiply by .5.  (Example: rate of $.50 x 12 units = $6.00 x .5 = $3.00 is the Price Rite rate).  The conversion is done based on the Wakefern contract.  When matching dates on the invoice to the contract, Price Rite has the approval to shift up to 3 weeks.  This would include the week before, the week of, or the week after.
General Information:
Wakefern’s policies for new item approval, item change, pricing guidelines, etc. can be reviewed in the Wakefern Supplier Guildelines document.

The GCC will step that portion as Invalid Other Escalate-Repay Issue regardless of the dollar amount (under tolerance would not be applied since we need to address this issue with the customer). On the DBW, enter the item, quantity, and the formula for the unsaleable amount in the rate field =Vend Price*.007, in this case =32.40*.007 which calculates as $54.43.  If the DBW extended amount for the item matches the extended amount on the customer invoice, it will be coded as unsaleable and escalated as a repay issue.
Please note there may be a trade portion along with the unsaleable portion. The example below is for this scenario.  There is a $1.20 off invoice along with the .7% unsaleable amount.
On the DBW, enter the item for the trade allowance as the first item, then enter the remainder amount as a second item for the unsaleable amount to confirm it is .7% of the Vend Price (enter the item, quantity, and the formula for the unsaleable amount in the rate field =Vend Price*.007, in this case =24.60*.007 which calculates as $51.66. In this example the trade portion equals $360.00 and the unsaleable portion $51.66.  The total for the two items on the DBW add up to $411.66 which matches the customer invoice extended amount. The trade portion would be stepped accordingly and the unsaleable portion would be split to a separate line and escalated as a repay issue.
Clip fees taken for digital coupons are approved for clearing even though they are not reflected on the contract.  They need to be cleared to the same coupon event that the digital coupon claim was cleared to, without an additional contract.
Campbells will not clear claims for in-store demos without detailed back up from the demo company.
The GCC needs to escalate for customer invoice.
The CRA needs to step to Request Backup from Sales.
The BMA will request a job number and the demo company backup from The Mars Agency.  The demo company backup will not be provided until 10 weeks post event.
Locked Cost deducctions do not get cleared with a contract.  The GCC/CCA should step to sales for an event number.  The BMA will get approval to clear with event from Campbell’s.
Claims for ISM labels are to be sent to sales for a contract.  The BMA will either provide the contract or get approval from Campbell’s to clear without a contract.

The CRA/BMA will add “CUST:4000000986” as a header note when assigning events for Zone 8.
For the “Must Buy” programs the smaller retailer may bill a portion of the allowance based on how many you must buy. As an example; The allowance may be “Must buy Two” with an allowance of $1.58. The smaller stores bill for that at the item level which because it’s must buy two would be half of the allowance $.79. Okay to proceed with validation without stepping to sales.

Once the open stock is received in Wakefern’s warehouse, Wakefern builds the pallets in their warehouse to be shipped to their stores.  Wakefern ships them to their stores as MM Punches/Ades MX Pallets.  Coke does not ship these mixed pallets to Wakefern.  The contracts will be for open stock and will not have the pallets on them.

The claim needs to be split as follows: 60% MM Punches 59oz and 40% MM Ades 59oz.  The customer invoice will only list one product but needs to be split into the two categories.

The raincheck fee is broken out to its own line and cleared to UT if it is below $250.00.  If the raincheck fee is more than $250.00, step to sales to advise.  The claim is to be broken down to mirror the DBW as per the client SOP.
Review the contract for the handling fee as it’s not always $.02 and it will need to be added to the scan unit rate as per below.
Example: Contract unit rate of $0.34 with handling fee of $0.02.
$0.34 + $0.02 = $0.36
When converted from units to cases, for a 6 pack product, the final rate would be $2.16; 8 pack would be $2.88; etc.
In some cases, there will be two events for one ad for the same dollar amount.  Place the cursor over each event number to get the brand code and dollar amount that is to be applied to each ad event #. The claim will need to be broken down per the events.
Invoices for Pickup Adjustment or Pickup Allowance mean that Wakefern is taking additional allowances that are usually not valid.  If the amount is greater than $250.00, these claims should be escalated to the CRA for research.  If the Pickup Adjustment / Allowance is below Coca-Cola’s tolerance of $250.00, the line can be stepped Unknown/Under Tolerance/Ready To Clear-CCA with a note “The Pickup Adjustment / Allowance is below tolerance”.
For claims which reference ‘Action Taken: DEDUCTION FOR PRICE’, if the difference between the Vend Price versus Our Price is $0.50/case or less, the claim should be stepped to Non-Trade/Damages/Unsaleables/Ready to Clear-CCA.  LINE NOTE: Notes must be entered referencing ARP-Swell Allowance for the item brand code which is claimed, the number of cases and the amount claimed. Example: ARP – Swell Allowance TR-Simply Orange 6/1.75LTR – 1600cs * $0.1603 = 256.48.  The CCA will follow the normal damage/unsaleable process for CCNA.  If a DBW is linked, the above item breakdown is not needed but the note is required to be entered stating ARP-Swell Allowance.
Difference of $.50 or lessDifference of $.50 or less

Pror to 1/1/23 claims for Logistical Support should be escalated to the CRA for processing. Claims will be cleared to OPEX and coded as Non-Trade / Shopper Marketing / RTC-CCA with the correct Client Event Name note for Merch/OPEX.

Do not required a contract.

Required an event number.

Require an event number

Reason Code select the correct reason code  majority should be PromoTrade.

A per case off invoice allowance is given to the customer as an automatic discount for product purchased from the client.  If the customer does not receive the allowance off the face of the invoice they will deduct for it.  If the customer requested an allowance that is not valid, the CSC will send a notification to the customer in writing. Customers view purchase orders as contracts. DBW Instructions for Price Plus:
2211BBAA33
Enter the UPCs using the product description (box 1).
Enter the quantity (box 3) on the invoice in the qty field in the DBW.
Enter the promo amount (box 2) from the invoice in the $ rate field of the DBW.
After all items are entered manually multiply the total quantity on the DBW by $.04* – hold this total until step 6.
Manually add the rain check total for each item – hold this total until step 6
Manually add the DBW total plus the total handling fee from step 4 and the total rain check fee from step 5.
If the total matches the invoice total – proceed to step 9.
If the total of the 3 amounts is more than the invoice total, proceed to step 7.
If the total of the 3 amounts is less than the invoice total, proceed to step 8.
Search for the contract and compare the rate on the contract to the rate on the invoice.
If they match, escalate to the CRA for invoice/DBW mismatch. (CRA – see BPS Team Info)
If they don’t match, update the DBW rate to match the contract rate – see the ‘Price Plus – Wakefern invest portion’ if this scenario applies. Add the new DBW total to the handling fee total (step 4) and the rain check total (step 5).
If the DBW totals now match the invoice total, proceed to step 9.
If the total of the 3 amounts is less than the invoice total, proceed to step 8.
Take the handling fee total from step 4 and multiply by 2.  Add this new handling fee total to the rain check total from step 5 and the DBW total. (See Handling Fee Note for additional details)
If they match, proceed to step 9.
If the total of the 3 amounts is less than the invoice total, complete the process in step 9 using the $.04* total from step 4 (not the doubled total from step 8) and proceed with validating the portion of the claim that the DBW totals. Escalate the difference between the DBW and the invoice for invoice/DBW mismatch.
Add the handling fee total (from step 4 or step 8, whichever applies) and the rain check total (from step 5) and divide by the DBW total. This new amount is now entered in the DBW Admin Fee % box. Click ‘update promotion total.’
The DBW total and the invoice total should now match – proceed with validation.
If they do not, check for entry or math errors – review above process.
* Handling Fee Note:
The handling fee is $0.04 for grocery and HBC/GM products.  The handling fee for perishable product is $0.08.  The handling fee for Barilla is $0.02.

CRA VALIDATION SPECIFIC
Price Plus invoice to DBW difference:
If a claim is escalated for step 7 (Contract & Invoice both have the same rate but the DBW total is still greater than claim total):
The CRA will double check for entry errors.
If no errors are found, the CRA will need to reach out to sales to work with Wakefern about the invoice total being greater than the deduction total.
If the claim is escalated for step 8b (Contract & Invoice rate match, plus calculating the handling fee at $.04 and the DBW total is still less than the claim total).
The GCC has gone back to the handling fee of $.02 on the lines that are validated and escalated the remaining balance.
The line that is escalated is not automatically a repay.
First the CRA will need to verify through sales if their client is being billed for the $.02 rate or $.04 for the handling fee.
If sales confirms that the customer is taking the $.04 handling rate, then the entire line amount is now a repay.
If sales confirms that the customer is taking the $.04 handling rate, go to step 4
The CRA will take the quantity from the DBW and multiply by $.02.  This total will now become valid and need to be stepped according to how the client handles promotional fees.
The remainder amount of the line that was escalated in step 8b is now the new repay total.

sections.title: CUSTOMER GENERAL INFORMATION
sections.content:
Customer Invoice Info:
Is line level detail indexed on the customer’s documentation (customer invoice, customer check request, unsalable/spoils, post audit, EDI 812/820 or client deduction notice if one of these documents is included)? Yes
Sometimes the Weis customer reference number will include additional verbiage.  When searching for the customer invoice, you only have to search using the numerical portion of the reference number.  For example, if the customer reference number is 63823809CREDIT, you only need to search for 63823809.  If the customer reference number is A/R246975-1NewStore, search only on 246975-1.
Weis customer invoice totals will generally not match the claim header amount because Weis factors in a discount amount.  To verify the claim amount against the customer invoice, you need both the customer invoice and the check remit.  Reference to the invoice number on the customer invoice:
Find the same customer invoice number on the check remit with the word CREDIT behind it and negative dollar amounts.
On the check remit column labeled Discount Amount, subtract the amount shown from the amount of the customer invoice.
The customer invoice amount minus the discount amount will equal the claim header amount.  Proceed with validating the claim.
Keep in mind that we are responsible for different types of claims for different clients.  For example, if the $1951.80 in this example includes $1393.80 in shortages, and we do not process shortages for that client, you will need to factor the difference ($558) minus the $41.29 discount amount, for an actual claim amount of $516.71.
STORE SHIPMENT RECAP billings:
Beginning in 2019, Weis will take scans as billbacks, based on shipments to the stores.  This applies to all ongoing scans EXCEPT those for clearance, discontinued items, and seasonal markdowns.
For contracts prior to April 2019 that show scans but are being converted to Store Shipment Report (SSR), follow the guideline by Weis of Sunday begin date 4 days prior to the start of performance and Saturday end date 3 days after end of performance.  For contracts from April 2019 forward, the dates are shown as Store Shipment Recap Dates.  These are the dates that are referenced on the customer invoice.
If the submitted contract was for unit scans, it will be invoiced as SSR units.  If the submitted contract was for case scans, it will be invoiced as SSR cases.
SECONDARY SUPPLY CHARGES
Per the attached policy letter, if Weis is unable to get product directly from a vendor due to out of stock, they will pull the product through C&S and deduct $1.00 per case for the product(s) that are procured from C&S.  This applies only to product that was bought through C&S because the vendor couldn’t fill Weis’ order.
DBW Info:
DBW with rounding issues
Oftentimes, Weis will round total amounts.  To ensure the DBW displays the correct amount, complete the case quantity fields and the total promotion amount fields.
Contract Info:
Prior to CY 2020, Weis contracts are done in Excel format, and the forms have multiple tabs.  The contract information will be found on the first tab.
For CY 2020 and forward, Weis contracts are generated via Aptaris.
Weis contracts end on Friday, and their billing period runs through Saturday of the same week.  If the billing end date is not more than one day after the contract end date, the contract can be used to validate the claim.
Other General Info:
POST AUDIT POLICY:
Weis’ statute of limitations for review of all contracts is four years.  Acosta policy is to disallow any post audit older than two years and pursue repayment.  For Weis, this becomes a policy vs policy.  Work with sales on next steps.

COCA COLA (CCNA)
New Store Fill deductions are cleared lump sums by brand, not by UPC.
CRA: Bracket Program (JBP) deductions: A breakdown must be requested from sales and the claim in AR broken down accordingly. Once the breakdown is received, approval must be requested from the CCNA FSM to clear without a contract and POP.
DOLE
Weis is an indirect of C&S for Dole Grocery & Frozen Warehouse 78. They are entitled to the SSA allowance/ crossroads agreement.
EDGEWELL Personal Care
Claims for discontinued items will not require a contract.
Retail merchandising Check Requests should be closed, customers will deduct.
Customer Check Requests will no longer be sent for Weis invoices, they will deduct through C&S.
There are some invoices that mention DSD, they are not actually DSD invoices and Acosta needs to handle. Do not close as unknown/Not Acosta.
EIGHT O’CLOCK COFFEE
Backup may be included with the check remit.  Find the check remit with a date that is near the claim date and then check all pages of the document to find the backup. If backup is not found, CRA will request it following the contact directions in the TATA SOP.
Coupon backup: Carolina Logistics/Inmar provides backup to the client.  Request Coupon claims Transfer to HQ and send to CCA for processing.  Trade Relations: 800-285-7602 for backup questions and issues.
HOSTESS
Damages/Unsaleable - No need to research Swell Allowances Off Invoice.
J.M. SMUCKERS
The C&S deductions or Count/Recount invoices received can be cleared to the same promo ID as the Weis OI deductions, please refer to the Event Detail Report for the promo id. When the customer invoice in the description states JBP and has "C&S" or "C&S Items" in the description that means it's for the JBP program for items sold to Weis from C&S. Weis is still entitled to the JBP allowances for products that they buy through C&S and is taking the allowance on indirect orders. The Events on the file will be Off Invoice type events when searching the event file. Select the event for the appropriate timeframe. You will need to confirm the allowance being billed which should match with the event list. If the Discount type on the event list is "% Off" it should match with the percentage on the Invoice. If the Discount type is $ Off you will need to calculate the appropriate allowance, you can do this by taking the total dollar value billed for the item and then dividing by the total units for that item. That will give you the rate that should match the event report.
KENS
Scheduling fee deductions are handled internally by Ken’s. Claims will be stepped as Non-Trade/Service Fee/Penalty with a clearing/math note stating “Scheduling fee – Ken’s handles internally”.
KRAFT
Ad deductions: Ad contracts will offer one amount. Weis will often create two invoices that total the allowance amount on the contract. Typically, invoices are not received at the same time. Review the VPF for additional ad deductions and continue validation. Example: contract offered a $3750 ad allowance; invoice XYZ billed $1000 and invoice ABC billed $2750; both deductions are valid if they do not exceed the $3750 allowance. If the allowances billed exceed the ad allowance offered, a partial repayment request will need to be written for the difference.
MARS
Weis is part of the Retail Merchandising Program.
MEZZETTA
Marketing fund claims:
Contract is not required.
Event numbers are required.
NEWELL BRANDS
Invoices for Markdowns/Discontinued do not require contracts.
NISSIN
PO Related claims with ship-to of C&S/Weis are handled internally by the client and should be closed as Not Acosta.
POMPEIAN
Weis Healthy Heart program invoices are to be coded as Non-trade/ Retail Merchandising.

1.Deduction Type: Off Invoice (OI)
A per case off invoice allowance (OI) is given to the customer as an automatic discount for product purchased from the client. If the customer does not receive the allowance off the face of the invoice they will deduct for it. If the customer requested an allowance that is not valid, the CSC will send a notification to the customer in writing. Customers view purchase orders as contracts. If they are not notified of allowance discrepancies, they will pay according to their purchase order total.

REPAY INFORMATION SECTION
INVALID PROCEDURE:
The below document contains the contact points for each department within Weis Accounting that issues vendor deductions. When disputing a deduction contact the department that generated the deduction as a starting point for the dispute. They will be able to further direct if their department requires solely their review or the involvement of a CM. Please also send to the Customer Manager.
INVALID POST AUDIT PROCEDURE:
If a post audit is found to be invalid and the invoice has been deducted, email all backup and the repay request to one of the following email addresses based on the invoice type and to the Customer Manager:
Invoices beginning with “S” claims@weismarkets.com
Invoice beginning with “WS” weis@ap-audit.com
PRGX audits weis@prgx.com
Invoice begins with “WS”: If the post audit is pre-notification and a backup request was submitted to weis@ap-audit.com   and log in information was provided, the audit can be disputed via the Claim Web Vendor Claim Page via the Dispute button. If the dispute option is not displayed and the only button option that is shown is “Update Contacts”, to dispute the claim an email will need to be submitted to the email noted above.
PRS/CRA Client Specific
Barilla America_Inc_Barilla_America_Wasa_Inc
The client manager should be copied on the repay request sent to the customer and customer manager.
CCA CLEARING INFORMATION SPECIFIC
CCA Client Specifics
BARILLA
SV deductions (supplier violations fees) can be cleared without the invoice. When clearing in Vistex, enter the clearing/math note provided by the GCC/CRA in Vistex which must state the follow: “violation type: (the compliance violation description that applies to the deduction) PO #: (the PO # that applies to the deduction)”.
DIAMOND
Promotional fees are cleared to the same promotional event; line level notes will be provided to show the promotion $ and fee $. This includes fees associated with the OI offers, these will normally be billed as a lump sum.
